name: London
note: 从乔叟到奥威尔，英语文学有一半写在这座城里：布莱克诗里“特许的街道”、约翰逊那句“厌倦了伦敦，就是厌倦了生活”、狄更斯《荒凉山庄》开篇的大雾、奥威尔笔下第一空降场的首都，写的都是它。今天街上的蓝色圆牌里，有许多标着作家住过的房子
note_en: From Chaucer to Orwell, a huge share of English literature is set in London: Blake's 'chartered streets', Dr Johnson's line 'When a man is tired of London, he is tired of life', the great fog at the start of Bleak House, the grim capital of Orwell's 1984. Today many of the blue plaques on its houses mark where writers lived

name: The Tabard, Southwark
name_zh: 南华克 · 泰巴德客栈旧址
note: 《坎特伯雷故事集》的出发点：二十九位朝圣者在泰巴德客栈过夜，店主哈里·贝利提议，一路上每人讲故事，讲得最好的回来白吃一顿晚饭。客栈是真实存在的，1873 年拆除，原址在博罗高街的塔尔博特院，墙上有纪念牌
note_en: This is where The Canterbury Tales begins. Twenty-nine pilgrims spend the night at the Tabard Inn, and the landlord, Harry Bailly, suggests they tell stories along the way, with a free supper for whoever tells the best one. The Tabard was a real inn. It was demolished in 1873, and a plaque now marks the spot in Talbot Yard, just off Borough High Street

name: Canterbury Cathedral
note: 1170 年大主教托马斯·贝克特在这座教堂里被国王的骑士刺杀，此后他的圣龛成了英格兰最重要的朝圣地，乔叟的朝圣者就是要来这里——虽然诗里他们一直没走到。圣龛 1538 年被亨利八世拆毁，原址点着一支蜡烛。《大卫·科波菲尔》里大卫也在坎特伯雷上学
note_en: In 1170, Archbishop Thomas Becket was murdered inside this cathedral by four of the king's knights. His shrine became the most important pilgrimage site in England, and it's where Chaucer's pilgrims are headed, although in the poem they never actually arrive. Henry VIII had the shrine destroyed in 1538, and a single candle now burns where it once stood. Canterbury is also where David Copperfield goes to school

name: Ely Place, Holborn
name_zh: 霍尔本 · 伊利府旧址
note: 莎士比亚把冈特的约翰临终那段著名独白放在这里：“这一个君王们的御座，这一个统于一尊的岛屿……这一片幸福的国土，这一个英格兰”。这里原是伊利主教的伦敦府邸，如今是一条有门禁的私家小街，街上的圣埃塞尔德丽达教堂和老酒馆“老主教冠”都有几百年历史
note_en: Shakespeare set John of Gaunt's famous dying speech here, the one that begins 'This royal throne of kings, this sceptred isle' and builds to 'This blessed plot, this earth, this realm, this England.' Ely Place was once the London palace of the Bishops of Ely. Today it's a quiet private street behind a gate, home to the medieval church of St Etheldreda and Ye Olde Mitre, a pub that has been here for centuries

name: Inverness
note: 莎士比亚把麦克白的城堡放在因弗内斯，国王邓肯就是在这里的客房里被刺杀的。真实的麦克白其实是在战场上杀死邓肯的，还当了十七年还算称职的国王。《古战场传奇》里，弗兰克和克莱尔也是在因弗内斯度蜜月的
note_en: Shakespeare placed Macbeth's castle at Inverness, and it's here that King Duncan is murdered in his sleep while a guest. The real Macbeth killed Duncan in battle and went on to rule Scotland, fairly competently, for seventeen years. In Outlander, Inverness is also where Frank and Claire spend their honeymoon

name: Birnam Wood
note: “除非勃南森林向邓西嫩高山移动，麦克白永远不会被打败。”女巫的预言最后应验：敌军砍下勃南森林的树枝作掩护向前推进。泰河边如今只剩一棵勃南橡树，据说是当年那片森林的最后一棵
note_en: 'Macbeth shall never vanquish'd be until / Great Birnam wood to high Dunsinane hill / Shall come against him.' The witches' prophecy comes true when the enemy army cuts branches from Birnam Wood and carries them as camouflage. One ancient tree, the Birnam Oak, still stands by the River Tay and is said to be the last survivor of that wood

name: Dunsinane Hill
note: 麦克白最后的据点，勃南森林“走”上山来的地方。锡德洛丘陵里这座山顶有一处铁器时代的山堡遗迹，当地一直叫它“麦克白城堡”。从山顶望出去，正能看见西北方向的勃南
note_en: This hill is Macbeth's last stronghold, where Birnam Wood comes marching up to meet him. At the top of Dunsinane Hill are the remains of an Iron Age fort that locals have long called Macbeth's Castle, and on a clear day you can look out towards Birnam to the north-west

name: St Paul's Cathedral
note: 马洛礼的《亚瑟王之死》里，石中剑出现在“伦敦最大的教堂”的院子里，传统上就是这里。现在的大教堂是 1666 年大火后雷恩重建的。老舍《二马》里，马家父子来伦敦接手的古玩铺就开在圣保罗教堂附近；布莱克的诗里，孩子们在升天节排队走进圣保罗
note_en: In Malory's Morte d'Arthur, the sword in the stone appears in the churchyard of 'the greatest church of London', which has traditionally been taken to mean St Paul's. The cathedral you see today was rebuilt by Christopher Wren after the Great Fire of 1666. In Lao She's Mr Ma and Son, the Mas come to London to run an antiques shop near St Paul's, and in one of William Blake's poems, charity children file into the cathedral on Holy Thursday

name: Scottish Highlands
note: “我的心在高原，我的心不在这里”——彭斯这首歌让苏格兰高地成了浪漫与乡愁的代名词，虽然他本人是低地人。司各特的诗和小说、史蒂文森《绑架》里大卫和艾伦的逃亡，都把读者带进这片山谷。今天沿西高地步道走一段，湖、荒原和峡谷还是书里的样子
note_en: 'My heart's in the Highlands, my heart is not here.' Burns's song made the Highlands a byword for romance and homesickness, though Burns himself was a Lowlander. Scott's poems and novels and David and Alan's flight in Stevenson's Kidnapped drew readers into these glens. Walk a stretch of the West Highland Way and the lochs, moors and passes look much as they do in the books

name: Westminster Bridge
note: “大地再没有比这更美的景色”：1802 年一个清晨，华兹华斯和妹妹坐马车经过威斯敏斯特桥，看见沉睡中的伦敦，写下这首十四行诗。他走过的老桥已经换掉，但从桥上望出去的泰晤士河和议会大厦还在
note_en: 'Earth has not anything to show more fair.' Early one morning in 1802, Wordsworth and his sister crossed Westminster Bridge by coach and saw London still asleep. He wrote this sonnet about the view. The bridge has since been rebuilt, but the view of the Thames and the Houses of Parliament is still there

name: Tintern Abbey
note: 1798 年 7 月华兹华斯和妹妹重游怀伊河谷，在修道院上游几英里的地方写下《廷特恩修道院》，这首诗成了《抒情歌谣集》的压轴之作，也是英国浪漫主义的宣言。修道院的哥特式废墟没有屋顶，至今立在河谷里
note_en: In July 1798, Wordsworth returned to the Wye Valley with his sister Dorothy and wrote the poem now known as 'Tintern Abbey' a few miles upriver. It was the final poem in Lyrical Ballads and became something like a manifesto for English Romanticism. The roofless Gothic ruins of the abbey still stand in the valley

name: The Cobb, Lyme Regis
name_zh: 莱姆里吉斯 · Cobb 堤岸
note: 《劝导》里路易莎·马斯格罗夫在这道防波堤的台阶上任性一跳，摔得不省人事，整个故事由此转向。据说丁尼生来莱姆时，别人要带他看蒙茅斯公爵登陆的地方，他说：别跟我提蒙茅斯公爵，带我去看路易莎摔下来的地方！这里也是《法国中尉的女人》里莎拉眺望大海的地方
note_en: In Persuasion, Louisa Musgrove jumps from the steps on this sea wall, falls and is knocked unconscious, and the whole story changes direction. When Tennyson visited Lyme and someone offered to show him where the Duke of Monmouth had landed, he supposedly said: 'Don't talk to me of the Duke of Monmouth. Show me the exact spot where Louisa Musgrove fell!' The Cobb is also where Sarah stands staring out to sea in The French Lieutenant's Woman

name: Lincoln's Inn
note: 《荒凉山庄》开篇，伦敦笼罩在大雾里，雾最浓的地方就是林肯律师学院大厅——大法官正坐在这里审一桩拖了几十年的遗产案“詹狄士诉詹狄士”。狄更斯年轻时在律师事务所当过小职员，熟悉这些法律迷宫
note_en: Bleak House opens in a thick London fog, and the fog is thickest of all here in Lincoln's Inn Hall, where the Lord Chancellor is presiding over Jarndyce and Jarndyce, an inheritance case that has dragged on for generations. As a young man Dickens had worked as a clerk in a law office, so he knew this legal maze from the inside

name: Edinburgh
note: 史蒂文森的家乡。他 1878 年写下《爱丁堡风物札记》，又爱又恨地描写这座“老烟城”：老城高耸的公寓楼、新城整齐的广场、终年不散的海风和雾
note_en: Edinburgh was Stevenson's hometown. In Edinburgh: Picturesque Notes, published in 1878, he wrote about 'Auld Reekie' with a mix of love and frustration: the towering tenements of the Old Town, the neat squares of the New Town, and the wind and sea mist that never seem to let up

name: Baker Street
note: 世界上最有名的虚构地址。柯南·道尔把福尔摩斯和华生的寓所放在贝克街 221B，当时街上并没有这个门牌。今天的贝克街地铁站墙上铺着福尔摩斯侧影的瓷砖，街北端有福尔摩斯博物馆
note_en: 221B Baker Street is the most famous fictional address in the world. When Conan Doyle put Holmes and Watson here, the number didn't even exist. Today the walls of Baker Street Underground station are tiled with Holmes's silhouette, and the Sherlock Holmes Museum sits at the north end of the street

name: Whitby Abbey
note: 1890 年布拉姆·斯托克在惠特比度假，在镇上图书馆的一本书里第一次读到“德古拉”这个名字。小说里德古拉乘坐的船在惠特比搁浅，他化作一条黑狗冲上岸，跑上通往修道院的 199 级台阶。修道院废墟至今立在东崖上，是哥特文学的朝圣地
note_en: In 1890 Bram Stoker was on holiday in Whitby when he came across the name 'Dracula' in a book at the town library. In the novel, Dracula's ship runs aground in Whitby's harbour, and he leaps ashore in the shape of a huge black dog and races up the 199 steps towards the abbey. The ruins still stand on the East Cliff, and they're a pilgrimage site for fans of Gothic fiction

name: Tower of London
note: 安斯沃思的历史小说《伦敦塔》写的是“九日女王”简·格雷的悲剧：十六岁被拥立为女王，九天后被废，1554 年在塔内的塔丘上被斩首。这座诺曼城堡做过王宫、监狱和刑场，如今还守着王冠珠宝和乌鸦
note_en: Harrison Ainsworth's novel The Tower of London tells the tragic story of Lady Jane Grey, the Nine Days' Queen. She was proclaimed queen at sixteen, overthrown just nine days later, and beheaded on Tower Green in 1554. Over the centuries this Norman fortress has been a royal palace, a prison and a place of execution, and it still guards the Crown Jewels and its famous ravens

name: Westminster · Big Ben
name_zh: 威斯敏斯特 · 大本钟
note: 《达洛维夫人》里，大本钟的钟声贯穿那个六月的一天：“先是一声警告，悦耳的；然后是报时，无可挽回的。铅色的圆圈在空中消散。”伍尔夫最初给这部小说起的名字就叫《时时刻刻》
note_en: Big Ben rings all through the single June day of Mrs Dalloway: 'First a warning, musical; then the hour, irrevocable. The leaden circles dissolved in the air.' Virginia Woolf's working title for the novel was The Hours

name: River Cam at King's College
note: “轻轻的我走了，正如我轻轻的来”：1928 年徐志摩重访剑桥，回国途中在船上写下《再别康桥》。诗里的金柳、青荇和“撑一支长篙”，都在国王学院这一段康河上。坐一趟撑篙船，就是走进这首诗
note_en: 'Quietly I take my leave, as quietly as I came here.' Xu Zhimo came back to Cambridge in 1928 and wrote Second Farewell to Cambridge on the voyage home to China. The golden willows, the waterweeds and the punt pole in the poem are all on this stretch of the Cam by King's College. Take a punt out and you're floating through the poem

name: St Giles' Churchyard, Stoke Poges
name_zh: 斯托克波吉斯 · 圣贾尔斯教堂墓园
prototype_of: 传统上认为是格雷《墓畔哀歌》里那座乡村墓园（学界没有定论）：“晚钟响起，白昼告终……”格雷常来这里看望葬在墓园里的母亲，去世后也葬在她身旁。教堂旁的田野里有一座纪念碑，刻着这首诗的诗句
prototype_of_en: This churchyard is traditionally thought to be the one in Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, though no one can say for certain. 'The curfew tolls the knell of parting day', it begins. Gray often came here to visit his mother's grave, and when he died he was buried next to her. In the field beside the church stands a monument carved with lines from the poem
coord_checked: Church of St Giles, Stoke Poges — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St_Giles,_Stoke_Poges, 2026-11-03

name: St Cross water meadows, Winchester
name_zh: 温彻斯特 · St Cross 水草甸
prototype_of: 诗中没有点名：1819 年 9 月济慈常沿这片水草甸散步，他写信告诉朋友，是星期天散步时看到的收割后的田野让他写下了这首诗；这条路线被普遍认为就是《秋颂》的风景
prototype_of_en: Keats never names the place in the poem, but in September 1819 he walked these water meadows every day, and in a letter to a friend he said the stubble fields he passed on his Sunday walk had made him write To Autumn. This route is widely taken to be the landscape of the poem

name: Top Withens, Haworth Moor
prototype_of: 常被和呼啸山庄联系在一起，主要是因为这里荒凉的高沼环境；不过废墟上勃朗特学会的牌子写明，这座农舍本身和艾米莉笔下的房子并不相像
prototype_of_en: This lonely ruined farmhouse on the moors is often linked with Wuthering Heights because of its bleak setting. But the Brontë Society's own plaque on the ruin points out that the building looked nothing like the house Emily described

name: Poets' Corner, Westminster Abbey
name_zh: 威斯敏斯特教堂 · 诗人角
note: 乔叟 1400 年葬在这里，是第一位葬在教堂的诗人，凭的其实是他当过王室工程总管；1599 年斯宾塞葬在他旁边，才有了“诗人角”的传统。今天这里葬着德莱顿、约翰逊、丁尼生、狄更斯、哈代和吉卜林，莎士比亚、弥尔顿、勃朗特三姐妹等人也有纪念碑
note_en: Chaucer was the first poet buried here, in 1400, and he owed it more to his job as clerk of the king's works than to his poetry. When Spenser was laid beside him in 1599, Poets' Corner was born. Dryden, Johnson, Tennyson, Dickens, Hardy and Kipling are buried here today, and Shakespeare, Milton and the Brontës are among the many writers with memorials

name: Shakespeare's Birthplace
note: 莎士比亚 1564 年生在斯特拉特福亨利街这座半木结构的房子里，在这里长大。两百多年来朝圣者络绎不绝，一扇窗玻璃上还留着沃尔特·司各特等访客刻下的名字。1847 年由公众募捐买下，是英国最早被保护起来的作家故居
note_en: Shakespeare was born in this half-timbered house on Henley Street in 1564 and spent his childhood here. Visitors have been making the pilgrimage for more than two hundred years, and one of the windows still carries names scratched into the glass by earlier fans, Walter Scott among them. The house was bought for the nation by public subscription in 1847, making it one of the first writers' homes in Britain to be preserved

name: Dove Cottage, Grasmere
note: 华兹华斯和妹妹多萝西 1799 至 1808 年住在这座小白屋里，这是他一生最多产的几年，《我孤独地漫游，像一朵云》也写于此时。多萝西在这里写的《格拉斯米尔日记》记下了那片水仙。后来《一个英国鸦片吸食者的自白》的作者德·昆西也搬进来住过
note_en: Wordsworth and his sister Dorothy lived in this little white cottage from 1799 to 1808, the most productive years of his life. I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud dates from this time, and the daffodils that inspired it first appear in Dorothy's Grasmere Journals, which she kept here. Later on, Thomas De Quincey, author of Confessions of an English Opium-Eater, moved in too

name: Keats House, Hampstead
name_zh: 汉普斯特德 · 济慈故居
note: 济慈 1818 至 1820 年住在这里，1819 年春天坐在花园里的李树下写出了《夜莺颂》。他在这里爱上了住在隔壁的芳妮·布劳恩，也是在这里第一次咳血，知道自己得了肺病。不久后他去罗马养病，二十五岁死在那里
note_en: Keats lived here from 1818 to 1820. One spring morning in 1819 he sat under a plum tree in the garden and wrote Ode to a Nightingale. This is also where he fell in love with Fanny Brawne, the girl next door, and where he first coughed up blood and realised he had tuberculosis. Soon afterwards he left for Rome, where he died at just twenty-five

name: Jane Austen's House, Chawton
name_zh: 乔顿 · 简·奥斯汀故居
note: 奥斯汀生命最后八年住在这座小屋里，修改出版了《理智与情感》《傲慢与偏见》，又写成《曼斯菲尔德庄园》《爱玛》和《劝导》。她在客厅一张十二边形的小桌上写作，据说故意不给门轴上油，门一响就把稿纸藏起来。小桌至今还在
note_en: Jane Austen spent the last eight years of her life in this cottage. Here she revised Sense and Sensibility and Pride and Prejudice for publication and wrote Mansfield Park, Emma and Persuasion. She worked at a tiny twelve-sided table in the sitting room, and the story goes that she left a creaky door unoiled so she'd hear visitors coming and have time to hide her pages. The table is still there

name: Brontë Parsonage Museum, Haworth
name_zh: 霍沃斯 · 勃朗特牧师住宅博物馆
note: 1820 年父亲帕特里克出任霍沃斯的牧师，勃朗特一家搬进这座牧师住宅。夏洛蒂、艾米莉和安妮一生大部分时间住在这里，周围的荒原贯穿她们的小说。1928 年起成为博物馆，由勃朗特学会管理
note_en: This was the Brontës' home from 1820, when their father Patrick became vicar of Haworth. Charlotte, Emily and Anne spent most of their lives here, and the moors that surround the house run all through their novels. It has been a museum, run by the Brontë Society, since 1928

name: Charles Dickens Museum
note: 狄更斯在伦敦住过的房子里唯一留存的一座。1837 至 1839 年他住在道蒂街 48 号，刚刚成名，在这里写完《匹克威克外传》，又写了《雾都孤儿》和《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》。他的书桌、手稿和家人的物品都陈列在这里
note_en: This is the only one of Dickens's London homes still standing. He moved into 48 Doughty Street in 1837, just as he was becoming famous, and while living here he finished The Pickwick Papers and wrote Oliver Twist and Nicholas Nickleby. His writing desk, manuscripts and family belongings are on display

name: Sherlock Holmes Museum
note: 柯南·道尔写福尔摩斯时，贝克街还没有 221B 这个门牌，几十年来寄给福尔摩斯的信都由街上的一家银行代为回复。如今这座博物馆挂着 221B 的门牌，按小说布置了福尔摩斯和华生的起居室，壁炉、小提琴和猎鹿帽一样不少
note_en: When Conan Doyle wrote the Sherlock Holmes stories, there was no such address as 221B Baker Street. For decades, letters addressed to Holmes were answered by a bank on the street. Today this museum proudly displays the 221B number and recreates Holmes and Watson's sitting room just as the stories describe it, right down to the violin and the deerstalker

name: Xu Zhimo poem stone, King's College
name_zh: 国王学院 · 徐志摩诗碑
note: 1921 至 1922 年徐志摩在国王学院读书，康河边的日子成了他一生的诗意源头。2008 年学院在康河边立起这块白色大理石诗碑，刻着《再别康桥》的首句和末句：“轻轻的我走了，正如我轻轻的来”。如今它是中国游客到剑桥必到的地方
note_en: The Chinese poet Xu Zhimo studied at King's College in 1921 and 1922, and his time by the River Cam shaped his poetry for the rest of his life. In 2008 the college placed this white marble stone on the riverbank, carved with the first and last lines of his Second Farewell to Cambridge: 'Quietly I take my leave, as quietly as I came here.' It has become a must-see for Chinese visitors to Cambridge

name: Lao She blue plaque, St James's Gardens
name_zh: 圣詹姆斯花园路 · 老舍故居蓝牌
note: 老舍 1925 至 1928 年在伦敦大学东方学院教中文，就住在圣詹姆斯花园路 31 号。他在这里写出了最早的三部长篇小说《老张的哲学》《赵子曰》和《二马》，后者写的正是伦敦华人的生活。2003 年这里挂上蓝牌，他是第一位获此纪念的中国作家
note_en: The Chinese novelist Lao She lived here from 1925 to 1928 while teaching Chinese at the University of London's School of Oriental Studies. In this house he wrote his first three novels, including Mr Ma and Son, a story about Chinese life in London. In 2003 he became the first Chinese writer to be honoured with an English Heritage blue plaque

name: Coastguard Cottages, Cuckmere Haven
name_zh: Cuckmere Haven · 海岸警卫队小屋（七姐妹白崖）
scene: 结局里罗比与塞西莉亚终于团聚的那座白崖下的海边小屋——电影最后揭示，这只是布里奥妮在小说里替他们写下的结局。小屋就在七姐妹白崖前，是英国海岸最经典的风景之一
scene_en: the white cottage by the sea where Robbie and Cecilia are finally together at the end of the film, a happy ending that turns out to exist only in the novel Briony writes for them. The cottages look out on the Seven Sisters, one of the most famous stretches of the English coast

name: Leadenhall Market
scene: 对角巷和破釜酒吧的入口。这座维多利亚时代的有顶市场被拍成了巫师购物街，市场边牛头巷里那扇蓝色的门（当时是一家眼镜店）就是破釜酒吧的门
scene_en: Diagon Alley and the entrance to the Leaky Cauldron. This ornate Victorian covered market played the wizards' shopping street, and a blue door just around the corner in Bull's Head Passage, an optician's shop at the time, became the entrance to the Leaky Cauldron

name: Christ Church, Oxford
name_zh: 牛津 · 基督教堂学院
scene: 麦格教授在楼梯口迎接一年级新生的那段扇形拱顶楼梯；学院的大礼堂也是电影里霍格沃茨礼堂的原型，后来在片场照样复制。这里也是刘易斯·卡罗尔任教的学院
scene_en: the fan-vaulted staircase where Professor McGonagall welcomes the first-years. The college's dining hall also inspired the Great Hall at Hogwarts, which was recreated in the studio. Christ Church is also where Lewis Carroll taught

name: Alnwick Castle
scene: 霍格沃茨的外景，哈利第一次骑扫帚的飞行课就在城堡外庭拍摄。城堡至今是诺森伯兰公爵家族的住所，夏天还在同一片草地上给游客开“飞行课”
scene_en: the outside of Hogwarts, including the castle grounds where Harry has his first flying lesson. Alnwick is still home to the Dukes of Northumberland, and in summer visitors can take their own broomstick lessons on the very same lawn

name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
scene: 霍格沃茨特快列车驶过这座 21 孔的弧形高架桥，《密室》里哈利和罗恩开着飞车追的也是这趟车。现实中“詹姆斯党人号”蒸汽火车夏天每天驶过，可以坐上去
scene_en: the Hogwarts Express crossing this curving, twenty-one-arch viaduct, the same train Harry and Ron chase in the flying car in Chamber of Secrets. In summer a real steam train, the Jacobite, crosses the viaduct every day, and you can ride it

name: Dyrham Park
scene: 达林顿府的外景：管家史蒂文斯服侍了一辈子的那座大宅，正门前的台阶和那条长长的车道都在这里拍。庄园建于 17 世纪末，如今属于国民信托，屋里还留着当年主人收藏的荷兰瓷器和画，园子里养着一群鹿
scene_en: the exterior of Darlington Hall, the great house Stevens has served all his life, with its front steps and long sweeping drive. Dyrham was built at the end of the seventeenth century and now belongs to the National Trust. Inside you can still see the Dutch delftware and paintings its first owner collected, and a herd of deer roams the park

name: Chalcot Crescent, Primrose Hill
scene: 布朗一家位于温莎花园 32 号的家，帕丁顿熊从秘鲁来到伦敦后就住在这里。樱草山这排五颜六色的房子本身就是伦敦最上镜的街景之一
scene_en: the Browns' house at 32 Windsor Gardens, where Paddington comes to live after arriving from Peru. With its row of brightly painted houses, this street in Primrose Hill is one of the most photographed in London
coord_checked: Numbers 24-46 and attached railings, Chalcot Crescent — https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1244108, 2026-11-03

name: Doune Castle
scene: 麦肯齐家族的利奥赫城堡，克莱尔穿越到 1743 年后第一个落脚的地方。这座 14 世纪城堡还拍过《权力的游戏》第一集的临冬城和《巨蟒与圣杯》
scene_en: Castle Leoch, home of Clan MacKenzie and the first place Claire finds shelter after falling back in time to 1743. The same fourteenth-century castle played Winterfell in the first episode of Game of Thrones, and it also turns up in Monty Python and the Holy Grail

name: Lindisfarne (Holy Island)
note: 《玛米恩》第二章，修女们乘船来到圣岛，司各特写潮水涨落之间这座岛时而是岛、时而连着陆地。635 年圣艾丹在这里建起修道院，著名的《林迪斯法恩福音书》就是这里的修士抄绘的。去岛上要看潮汐表走堤道
note_en: In the second canto of Marmion, a group of nuns sail to Holy Island, and Scott describes how the tides make it an island one moment and part of the mainland the next. St Aidan founded a monastery here in 635, and its monks created the Lindisfarne Gospels. To get there today, you still have to check the tide tables before driving across the causeway

name: Bamburgh Castle
note: 司各特在《玛米恩》里写诺森伯兰海岸，修女们的船从班堡城堡下驶过。城堡立在海边的玄武岩高台上，曾是古诺森布里亚王国的王都，至今是英格兰最壮观的海边城堡之一
note_en: In Marmion, the nuns' ship sails past Bamburgh on its way down the Northumberland coast. The castle sits on a great outcrop of volcanic rock above the beach. It was once the royal seat of the kingdom of Northumbria, and it's still one of the most spectacular coastal castles in England

name: Glencoyne Bay, Ullswater
name_zh: 阿尔斯沃特湖 · 格伦科因湾
prototype_of: 诗中没有点名：1802 年 4 月 15 日华兹华斯兄妹在这段湖岸看见成片的水仙，多萝西的日记记下了这一天，两年后华兹华斯写成这首诗
prototype_of_en: Wordsworth doesn't name the place in the poem, but on 15 April 1802 he and his sister Dorothy saw the daffodils growing along this shore, as Dorothy recorded in her journal. He wrote I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud two years later

name: Manchester
prototype_of: 《南方与北方》里工业城米尔顿的原型。盖斯凯尔是牧师的妻子，在曼彻斯特住了一辈子，亲眼看着这座“棉都”的工厂主和工人对立，把这一切写进了小说。她的故居也在城里
prototype_of_en: Manchester is the model for Milton, the industrial city in North and South. Elizabeth Gaskell, the wife of a Unitarian minister, lived here for her whole married life. She saw the conflict between factory owners and workers in 'Cottonopolis' first-hand and put it at the heart of her novel. Her house in the city is now a museum

name: Erewash valley near Cossall
name_zh: 埃瑞瓦什河谷 · 科索尔附近
note: 《虹》里布朗文一家世代耕种的玛什农场就在埃瑞瓦什河谷，小说里的科塞西村以科索尔为原型。劳伦斯在几英里外的伊斯特伍德长大，管这一带叫“我心中的乡野”
note_en: In The Rainbow, generations of the Brangwen family farm the Marsh Farm here in the Erewash Valley, and the village of Cossethay in the novel is based on Cossall. D. H. Lawrence grew up a few miles away in Eastwood and called this 'the country of my heart'
coord_checked: Cossall (Wikipedia, via wikwiand mirror; also List of UK locations Cos-Cou) — https://wikwiand-revamp.pages.dev/en/Cossall, 2026-11-03

name: Bredon Hill
note: “夏日在布雷登山上，钟声那样清朗”——《什罗普郡少年》里一对恋人在山上听教堂钟声。豪斯曼其实不是什罗普郡人，他在伍斯特郡长大，望着西边地平线上那些“蓝色的记忆中的山丘”写下了这本诗集
note_en: 'In summertime on Bredon / The bells they sound so clear.' In this poem from A Shropshire Lad, two lovers lie on the hill listening to church bells. Housman wasn't actually from Shropshire. He grew up in Worcestershire, gazing west at the 'blue remembered hills' on the horizon, and wrote this book about them

name: Wenlock Edge
note: “温洛克岭上的树林不安宁”：豪斯曼把古罗马人曾经看过的同一阵风吹进了这首诗。这道二十多公里长的林木陡崖后来因沃恩·威廉斯把组诗谱成声乐套曲《在温洛克岭上》而更加出名
note_en: 'On Wenlock Edge the wood's in trouble.' In Housman's poem, the same wind that once troubled the Romans is still blowing through the trees. This long wooded ridge became even more famous when Vaughan Williams set the poems to music in his song cycle On Wenlock Edge

name: Clun
note: “克伦顿和克伦伯里，克伦冈福德和克伦，是太阳底下最安静的地方”——豪斯曼在诗前引用了这首当地古老的童谣。克伦是威尔士边境的一座小镇，有一座诺曼城堡废墟
note_en: 'Clunton and Clunbury, / Clungunford and Clun, / Are the quietest places / Under the sun.' Housman borrowed this old local rhyme to introduce one of his poems. Clun is a small town near the Welsh border, with the ruins of a Norman castle

name: Ludlow
note: 两位诗人在这里相遇。1634 年弥尔顿的假面剧《科摩斯》在拉德洛城堡首演；两百多年后，豪斯曼在《什罗普郡少年》里写小伙子们赶集来到拉德洛，他死后骨灰也葬在镇上圣劳伦斯教堂的墙外
note_en: Two poets meet in Ludlow. Milton's masque Comus was first performed at Ludlow Castle in 1634. More than two centuries later, the young men in Housman's A Shropshire Lad come here for the fair. Housman's ashes are buried against the wall of St Laurence's Church in the town

name: Giant's Causeway
note: 约四万根六角形玄武岩柱一直伸进海里，传说是巨人芬恩为了渡海去苏格兰而铺的路。约翰逊博士对它的评价很有名：“值得一看？是的；值得专程去看？不。”萨克雷在《爱尔兰札记》里也写了这里
note_en: Around forty thousand hexagonal basalt columns step down into the sea here. Legend says they're the remains of a road the giant Finn McCool built so he could walk across to Scotland. Dr Johnson's verdict on the place is famous: 'Worth seeing? Yes; but not worth going to see.' Thackeray also wrote about it in The Irish Sketch Book

name: Belfast
note: 1842 年萨克雷环游爱尔兰，在《爱尔兰札记》里写下了当时正在兴起的工业城市贝尔法斯特。这座城后来造出了泰坦尼克号，也是 C. S. 刘易斯和谢默斯·希尼求学的地方
note_en: Thackeray toured Ireland in 1842, and in The Irish Sketch Book he described Belfast as a busy industrial town on the rise. The city would later build the Titanic. It's also where C. S. Lewis grew up and where Seamus Heaney went to university

name: Chatsworth House
prototype_of: 常被认为是《傲慢与偏见》彭伯里庄园的原型。小说里伊丽莎白游德比郡时专门提到去了查茨沃斯，接着就去了彭伯里；2005 年的电影直接在这里拍了彭伯里，雕塑廊里还摆着电影里的达西胸像
prototype_of_en: Chatsworth is often said to be the model for Pemberley, Mr Darcy's estate in Pride and Prejudice. In the novel, Elizabeth mentions visiting Chatsworth on her tour of Derbyshire just before she goes to Pemberley. The 2005 film used Chatsworth as Pemberley, and the bust of Darcy from the film is still on display in the sculpture gallery

name: Brighton
note: 《傲慢与偏见》里莉迪亚跟着民兵团去了布莱顿，在那里和威克姆私奔，差点毁了整个班纳特家。摄政王在这里建了富丽的英皇阁，让布莱顿成了当时最时髦也最轻佻的海滨城市
note_en: In Pride and Prejudice, Lydia follows the army regiment to Brighton, where she runs off with Wickham and almost ruins her whole family. The Prince Regent built his extravagant Royal Pavilion here, which made Brighton the most fashionable, and most scandalous, seaside resort of its day

name: Box Hill
note: 《爱玛》里最让人难堪的一幕：大家在博克斯山野餐，爱玛当众取笑了善良唠叨的贝茨小姐，奈特利先生事后严厉地责备了她，她第一次真正为自己羞愧。山顶视野开阔，至今是伦敦人周末徒步的地方
note_en: Box Hill is the setting for the most painful scene in Emma. At a picnic on the hill, Emma makes fun of kind, chatty Miss Bates in front of everyone, and when Mr Knightley tells her off afterwards, she feels truly ashamed of herself for the first time. The views from the top still draw walkers out from London every weekend

name: Bath
note: 《诺桑觉寺》和《劝导》都发生在巴斯，凯瑟琳在这里第一次进入社交场。奥斯汀本人 1801 至 1806 年住在巴斯，并不怎么喜欢它。这座乔治王时代的温泉城整体是世界遗产，每年秋天办简·奥斯汀节
note_en: Northanger Abbey and Persuasion are both set in Bath, and it's where Catherine makes her first entrance into society. Austen lived in Bath herself from 1801 to 1806 and never much liked it. The whole Georgian spa city is now a World Heritage Site, and it hosts a Jane Austen Festival every autumn

name: Beechen Cliff, Bath
note: 《诺桑觉寺》里凯瑟琳和蒂尔尼兄妹爬上比琴崖散步，亨利给她讲了一通如皮画式风景的理论。她学得太认真，最后把整座巴斯城都判为不配入画。从崖顶看下去的巴斯全景至今还是最好的
note_en: In Northanger Abbey, Catherine climbs Beechen Cliff with Henry and Eleanor Tilney, and Henry gives her a lecture on picturesque scenery. She takes it all so seriously that she ends up deciding the whole city of Bath isn't pretty enough to be part of a landscape. The view of Bath from the top is still the best you'll find
coord_checked: Beechen Cliff, Bath and North East Somerset — https://britishplacenames.uk/beechen-cliff-bath-and-north-east-somerset-st748640/maps, 2026-11-03

name: The Pump Room, Bath
note: 乔治王时代巴斯社交的中心：人们来这里喝温泉水，更为了看人和被人看。《匹克威克外传》里匹克威克先生一行来这里应酬，奥斯汀的人物也在这里相遇。今天大厅仍是餐厅，还能尝一杯温泉水
note_en: In Georgian Bath, the Pump Room was the centre of social life. People came to drink the spa water, but mostly they came to see and be seen. Mr Pickwick and his friends make the rounds here, and Austen's characters run into each other here too. The room is still a restaurant today, and you can still try a glass of the water

name: Rochester Castle
note: 《匹克威克外传》第二章，匹克威克先生一行从伦敦来到罗切斯特，在城堡废墟前听金格尔先生连珠炮似地胡侃。狄更斯童年在附近的查塔姆度过，晚年住在不远的盖兹山庄，罗切斯特在他的书里一再出现，最后一部小说《德鲁德疑案》也发生在这里
note_en: In chapter two of The Pickwick Papers, Mr Pickwick and his friends arrive in Rochester and listen to Mr Jingle's non-stop chatter beneath the castle ruins. Dickens spent part of his childhood in nearby Chatham and his final years at Gad's Hill, just outside town. Rochester turns up again and again in his books, and his last, unfinished novel, The Mystery of Edwin Drood, is set here

name: Great Yarmouth
note: 《大卫·科波菲尔》里佩格蒂一家住在雅茅斯海滩上一条倒扣的旧船里，小大卫觉得这是世界上最奇妙的房子，也在这里遇见了小艾米莉。后来那场夺走斯蒂尔福思和汉姆的风暴也发生在这片海上
note_en: In David Copperfield, the Peggotty family live on the beach at Yarmouth in an old boat turned upside down, which young David thinks is the most wonderful house in the world. It's here that he first meets little Em'ly. Later, the storm that drowns Steerforth and Ham strikes off this same coast

name: Preston
prototype_of: 常被认为是《艰难时世》焦煤镇的原型。1854 年普雷斯顿的纺织工人与厂主僵持了半年多，狄更斯专程来看，回去后把烟囱、红砖和黑色的运河都写进了焦煤镇
prototype_of_en: Preston is often said to be the model for Coketown in Hard Times. In 1854 the town's cotton workers were locked in a months-long dispute with the mill owners. Dickens came up to see it for himself and put the chimneys, the red brick and the black canal into his portrait of Coketown

name: St James' Church, Cooling
name_zh: 库林 · 圣詹姆斯教堂
prototype_of: 《远大前程》开篇沼地墓园的原型：小匹普在父母的墓前被逃犯马格韦契一把抓住。教堂墓园里至今排着一行小小的菱形墓石，是同一家夭折的孩子们的，狄更斯把它们写成了匹普五个早夭兄弟的墓
prototype_of_en: This marshland churchyard is the model for the opening of Great Expectations, where little Pip is grabbed by the escaped convict Magwitch beside his parents' grave. A row of small lozenge-shaped headstones still lies here, marking the graves of children from one family who all died young. Dickens turned them into the graves of Pip's five little brothers

name: Knutsford
prototype_of: 《克兰福德》的原型：盖斯凯尔在这座柴郡小镇长大，书里那些精打细算、恪守体面的老小姐们都有这里的影子。她去世后葬在镇上布鲁克街礼拜堂的墓园
prototype_of_en: Knutsford is the model for Cranford. Elizabeth Gaskell grew up in this small Cheshire town, and the book's genteel, penny-pinching ladies all have a little of Knutsford in them. She's buried here, in the graveyard of the Brook Street Chapel

name: Gainsborough
prototype_of: 《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》圣奥格镇的原型。乔治·艾略特为了写小说结尾那场洪水，专程来看特伦特河上的涌潮，这座河边小镇和它的仓库、码头就成了麦琪和汤姆的家乡
prototype_of_en: Gainsborough is the model for St Ogg's in The Mill on the Floss. While planning the flood at the end of the novel, George Eliot came here to see the tidal bore on the River Trent, and this riverside town, with its warehouses and wharves, became Maggie and Tom's home

name: Blackmore Vale
note: 苔丝的故乡。哈代称它为“小牛奶场谷”，一片被丘陵环抱的肥沃谷地，苔丝就生在谷里的马洛特村。小说开篇她在五月节的游行里第一次遇见安吉尔·克莱尔，那时一切还没有开始
note_en: This is Tess's home country. Hardy called it the Vale of the Little Dairies, a rich green valley surrounded by hills, and Tess is born in the village of Marlott. At the start of the novel, she first notices Angel Clare at the village May Day dance, before any of her troubles begin

name: Stonehenge
note: 《德伯家的苔丝》的结局：逃亡的苔丝和安吉尔夜里走到巨石阵，她躺在一块祭坛石上睡着了。天亮时警察围了上来，她醒来说：“我准备好了。”这是英国文学里最令人难忘的结尾之一
note_en: Tess of the d'Urbervilles ends here. On the run, Tess and Angel reach Stonehenge in the dark, and she falls asleep on one of the great stones. At dawn the police close in. She wakes up and says simply, 'I am ready.' It's one of the most haunting endings in English literature

name: Dartmoor
note: 《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》的舞台：荒凉的花岗岩高沼、吞人的格林盆泥沼、夜里传来的猎犬嚎叫。1901 年柯南·道尔住在高沼上的王子镇，跟着向导走遍了这片沼地。达特穆尔监狱也在这里
note_en: Dartmoor is the setting for The Hound of the Baskervilles, with its bleak granite moorland, the deadly Grimpen Mire, and a hound howling in the night. In 1901 Conan Doyle stayed in Princetown, right in the middle of the moor, and explored it with a local guide. Dartmoor Prison is here too

name: Erraid
note: 《绑架》里大卫·巴尔弗以为自己被困在一座荒岛上，挨饿挨了四天，最后才发现退潮时就能走回马尔岛。这座小岛是真实的：史蒂文森年轻时随父亲来岛上的灯塔工地，后来把这段经历写进了小说
note_en: In Kidnapped, David Balfour thinks he's shipwrecked on a deserted island and goes hungry for four days, before he realises that at low tide he could have simply walked across to Mull. Erraid is a real island. As a young man, Stevenson came here with his father, who was building a lighthouse offshore, and he later used the experience in the novel

name: South Queensferry
note: 《绑架》里，大卫的伯父埃比尼泽在昆斯费里的霍斯客栈和船长密谋，把他骗上船卖到海外；据说史蒂文斯就是住在这家客栈时开始构思这部小说的。客栈至今还在营业，就在福斯铁路桥脚下，站在岸边能同时看到横跨福斯湾的三座大桥
note_en: In Kidnapped, David's wicked uncle Ebenezer meets a sea captain at the Hawes Inn in Queensferry and plots to have David shipped off and sold overseas, and Stevenson is said to have started the novel while staying at the inn. It's still open, right under the Forth Bridge, and from the shore you can see all three bridges across the Firth of Forth

name: Hampton Court maze
note: 《三怪客泛舟记》里最好笑的一段：哈里斯自信满满地带大家走迷宫，说只要一直右转十分钟就能出来，结果越走越多人跟着他，最后全体迷路，只能等管理员来救。这座树篱迷宫种于 17 世纪 90 年代，是英国现存最老的
note_en: This is the setting for one of the funniest scenes in Three Men in a Boat. Harris confidently leads the way into the maze, insisting that you just keep turning right and you'll be out in ten minutes. More and more people follow him, until the whole crowd is hopelessly lost and has to be rescued by the keeper. Planted in the 1690s, it's the oldest surviving hedge maze in Britain

name: Marlow
note: 《三怪客泛舟记》里三个人和一条狗划船经过马洛，杰罗姆称赞这是泰晤士河上最热闹可爱的小镇之一。早几十年，雪莱夫妇也在镇上住过，玛丽·雪莱在这里写完了《弗兰肯斯坦》
note_en: In Three Men in a Boat, the three friends and their dog row past Marlow, and Jerome calls it one of the liveliest and prettiest towns on the Thames. A few decades earlier, Percy and Mary Shelley lived here, and Mary finished writing Frankenstein in the town

name: Iffley Lock
note: 《三怪客泛舟记》里三怪客划到牛津附近，在泰晤士河的船闸前排队等着过闸。这是牛津下游最美的船闸之一，旁边就是一座 12 世纪的诺曼式教堂
note_en: Near the end of their trip up the Thames, the three men in Three Men in a Boat wait their turn at the locks just below Oxford. Iffley is one of the prettiest of them, with a twelfth-century Norman church just beside it

name: Eastwood
prototype_of: 《儿子与情人》里贝斯特伍德的原型。劳伦斯 1885 年生在这座矿工小镇，父亲是矿工，母亲出身体面、一心想让儿子出人头地——小说里莫雷尔一家就是他自己的家。镇上有他的出生地博物馆
prototype_of_en: Eastwood is the model for Bestwood in Sons and Lovers. D. H. Lawrence was born in this mining town in 1885. His father was a miner, and his mother, who came from a more respectable family, was determined her sons would do better. The Morel family in the novel is really Lawrence's own. The house where he was born is now a museum

name: Sherwood Forest
note: 罗宾汉和他的快乐伙伴们的绿林。霍华德·派尔 1883 年的《罗宾汉的快乐冒险》把这些民谣故事讲给了全世界的孩子。森林里那棵“大橡树”有八百到一千岁，传说是罗宾汉一伙的藏身处
note_en: Sherwood is the greenwood of Robin Hood and his Merry Men. Howard Pyle's The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood, published in 1883, retold the old ballads for children all over the world. The forest's Major Oak, somewhere between eight hundred and a thousand years old, is said to have been the outlaws' hideout

name: Iona
note: 563 年圣科伦巴从爱尔兰来到这座小岛，从这里把基督教传遍苏格兰。1773 年约翰逊和鲍斯韦尔来到岛上，约翰逊写下了一句名言：一个人站在艾奥纳的废墟中，如果虔诚之心不会更加炽热，那就不值得羡慕
note_en: In 563 St Columba sailed here from Ireland and began spreading Christianity across Scotland from this tiny island. When Dr Johnson and Boswell landed here in 1773, Johnson wrote one of his most famous sentences: anyone whose faith 'would not grow warmer among the ruins of Iona' was not a man to be envied

name: Loch Ness
note: 1773 年约翰逊和鲍斯韦尔骑马沿着尼斯湖南岸北上，约翰逊在《苏格兰西部群岛旅行记》里写湖水、山坡和路边的茅屋，对水怪只字未提——尼斯湖水怪的传说要到 1933 年才火起来
note_en: In 1773 Johnson and Boswell rode along the shore of Loch Ness on their way north. In his Journey to the Western Islands of Scotland, Johnson describes the water, the hillsides and a little hut by the road, but says nothing at all about a monster. The legend of the Loch Ness Monster didn't really take off until 1933

name: Shakespeare Cliff, Dover
name_zh: 多佛尔 · 莎士比亚崖
note: 《李尔王》里最动人的一场：瞎了眼的葛罗斯特想从多佛尔悬崖跳下去，儿子埃德加假装带他到崖边，描绘了一番令人眩晕的高度，其实他只是在平地上扑倒。这座白垩崖因此被叫作莎士比亚崖
note_en: This is the setting of one of the most moving scenes in King Lear. The blinded Gloucester wants to throw himself off the cliffs at Dover, so his son Edgar pretends to lead him to the edge and describes a dizzying drop below. In fact they're standing on flat ground, and Gloucester simply falls forward. The cliff has been known as Shakespeare Cliff ever since

name: Dover
note: 英国面对欧洲的大门，多少小说里的人物从这里渡海：达达尼昂来追钻石坠子，《双城记》里的人们往返巴黎和伦敦。马修·阿诺德的《多佛海滩》据说写于他 1851 年蜜月途经多佛尔时：退潮的“信仰之海”发出长长的、退却的呼啸
note_en: Dover has always been England's doorway to Europe, and countless characters cross the Channel from here, from d'Artagnan chasing the queen's diamond studs to the travellers of A Tale of Two Cities. Matthew Arnold is thought to have written Dover Beach while on his honeymoon here in 1851, listening to the 'long, withdrawing roar' of the Sea of Faith

name: Grantchester
note: “教堂的钟还停在三点差十分吗？下午茶时还有蜂蜜吗？”1912 年鲁珀特·布鲁克在柏林想念剑桥郊外这个小村，写下《格兰切斯特的老牧师住宅》。村里的果园茶园从 1897 年开到现在，布鲁克和伍尔夫、凯恩斯都在这里喝过茶
note_en: 'Stands the Church clock at ten to three? / And is there honey still for tea?' In 1912, homesick in a Berlin café, Rupert Brooke wrote The Old Vicarage, Grantchester about this little village outside Cambridge. The Orchard tea garden has been serving tea here since 1897, and Brooke, Virginia Woolf and John Maynard Keynes all spent afternoons in it

name: Loch Katrine
note: 1810 年司各特的长诗《湖上夫人》出版，卡特琳湖一夜之间成了游览胜地，苏格兰高地旅游由此开始。湖上至今有一艘 1900 年的蒸汽船，名字就叫“沃尔特·司各特爵士号”
note_en: When Walter Scott published The Lady of the Lake in 1810, Loch Katrine became a tourist attraction almost overnight, and Highland tourism was born. A steamship built in 1900 still carries visitors across the loch. Its name is the Sir Walter Scott

name: Oxford
note: 马修·阿诺德称它为“梦幻尖塔之城”。这座大学城写进了太多书：弗兰肯斯坦和朋友在这里游历，《故园风雨后》里查尔斯在这里遇见塞巴斯蒂安，霍普金斯在这里写下他的诗。城里的学院、书店和酒馆处处是文学地标
note_en: Matthew Arnold called Oxford 'that sweet city with her dreaming spires'. The university town turns up in countless books. Victor Frankenstein and his friend visit it, Charles meets Sebastian here in Brideshead Revisited, and Gerard Manley Hopkins wrote some of his poems here. Its colleges, bookshops and pubs are packed with literary history

name: Elwy valley
note: 1874 至 1877 年霍普金斯在河谷上方的圣伯诺学院修习神学，这是他诗歌最丰收的时期，《茶隼》《斑驳之美》都写于此时。他还专门写了一首《在埃尔威河谷》
note_en: From 1874 to 1877 Gerard Manley Hopkins studied for the priesthood at St Beuno's College, high above this valley. These were his richest years as a poet: The Windhover and Pied Beauty both date from this time, and he even wrote a poem called In the Valley of the Elwy

name: Burslem
prototype_of: 本涅特“五镇”小说里伯斯利的原型。伯斯勒姆是英格兰陶瓷业的发源地，被称作“陶都之母”，本涅特在这里长大，《老妇谭》写的就是这里布店老板一对姐妹的一生
prototype_of_en: Burslem is the model for Bursley in Arnold Bennett's novels of the Five Towns. Known as the 'Mother Town' of the Potteries, it's where Bennett grew up, and The Old Wives' Tale follows the lives of a local draper's two daughters here

name: Bateman's and Pook's Hill, Burwash
name_zh: 伯沃什 · 贝特曼斯与普克山
note: 《普克山的帕克》里，丹和尤娜在仲夏夜的草地上演《仲夏夜之梦》，召唤出了小精灵帕克，帕克又带来了这片土地上几千年里的人物。那片草地和山坡就在吉卜林的贝特曼庄园对面，从他书房的窗户就能看到
note_en: In Puck of Pook's Hill, two children, Dan and Una, act out A Midsummer Night's Dream in a meadow on Midsummer Eve and accidentally summon Puck. He brings them people from thousands of years of English history. The meadow and the hill are just across from Kipling's house, Bateman's, and he could see them from his study window

name: Snowdon
note: 威尔士最高峰。1854 年乔治·博罗徒步走遍威尔士，在《狂野的威尔士》里写了他和女儿登上斯诺登峰顶的情景，还在峰顶用威尔士语高声背诵诗歌
note_en: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales. On his walking tour of Wales in 1854, George Borrow climbed it with his stepdaughter, and in Wild Wales he describes standing on the summit and reciting Welsh poetry at the top of his voice

name: Llangollen
note: 乔治·博罗 1854 年以兰戈伦为大本营，在这里学威尔士语、跟当地人聊天，然后出发徒步。《狂野的威尔士》就从这里写起。迪河谷小镇如今以每年的国际音乐节闻名
note_en: In 1854 George Borrow made Llangollen his base, practising his Welsh with the locals before setting off on foot across the country. Wild Wales begins here. Today this town in the Dee Valley is best known for its International Eisteddfod, a music festival held every summer

name: Doone Valley, Badgworthy Water
name_zh: 杜恩谷 · 巴奇沃西溪
note: 《洛娜·杜恩》里杜恩家族强盗的藏身谷。主人公约翰·里德少年时顺着溪水逆流而上，爬上瀑布，第一次在这里遇见了洛娜。从马尔斯福德沿巴奇沃西溪走上去，就是小说里那条路
note_en: This hidden valley is the hideout of the outlaw Doone family in Lorna Doone. As a boy, John Ridd climbs up the stream and a slippery waterfall and meets Lorna here for the first time. If you walk up Badgworthy Water from Malmsmead, you're following his route
coord_checked: MDE1258 - Deserted medieval settlement at Badgworthy Water - Exmoor HER — https://www.exmoorher.co.uk/Monument/MDE1258, 2026-11-03

name: Norham Castle
note: 司各特的长诗《玛米恩》开头第一句：“夕阳落在诺勒姆陡峭的城堡上。”这座边境城堡守着特威德河，几百年里反复被苏格兰人围攻。透纳也画过好几次这里的日出
note_en: Walter Scott's long poem Marmion opens with the line 'Day set on Norham's castle steep.' This border castle guarded the River Tweed and was attacked by the Scots again and again over the centuries. Turner painted it at sunrise several times

name: Hadrian's Wall at Housesteads
name_zh: 哈德良长城 · 豪斯斯特兹
note: 《普克山的帕克》里，帕克唤来的罗马百夫长帕内修斯讲他驻守哈德良长城的故事：风、雾、北方的皮克特人。豪斯斯特兹是长城上保存最好的罗马要塞，站在城墙上能看见长城在山脊上起伏
note_en: In Puck of Pook's Hill, Puck summons a Roman centurion named Parnesius, who tells the children about his time guarding Hadrian's Wall: the wind, the fog, and the Picts lurking to the north. Housesteads is the best-preserved Roman fort on the Wall, and from its ramparts you can watch the Wall rise and fall along the ridge

name: Tynemouth Priory
note: 《玛米恩》里修女们的船驶过泰恩河口，经过岬角上的修道院和城堡废墟。这座修道院几百年来也是海员的地标，诺森布里亚的几位国王葬在这里
note_en: In Marmion, the nuns' ship sails past the mouth of the River Tyne, where the ruined priory and castle stand on the headland. For centuries the priory was a landmark for sailors, and several kings of Northumbria were buried here

name: Corrymellagh (Corrymeela), near Cushendun
name_zh: 库申登附近 · 科里米拉（Corrymellagh）
note: 莫伊拉·奥尼尔的《科里米拉》写一个流落他乡的人想念安特里姆山谷的家，是《安特里姆山谷之歌》里最有名的一首。这个地名只有库申登附近这一处，诗里没有说明指哪里，这是最可能的解读
note_en: Moira O'Neill's Corrymeela, the best-known poem in her Songs of the Glens of Antrim, is about someone far from home longing for this place. The only Corrymeela on the map is this one near Cushendun, where she grew up. The poem doesn't say exactly where it means, but this is the most likely spot
coord_checked: Corrymellagh townland, Culfeightrin parish (gazetteer.org.uk GBPN326462, Irish grid D 2542 3518; same point on townlands.ie) — https://gazetteer.org.uk/place/Corrymellagh_TD,_Antrim_326462, 2026-11-04

name: Carrickfergus Castle
note: 萨克雷在《爱尔兰札记》里经过这座诺曼城堡。它 1177 年开始建，是爱尔兰保存最好的中世纪城堡之一，三面临海。民谣《卡里克弗格斯》唱的就是这里
note_en: Thackeray passes this Norman castle in The Irish Sketch Book. Building began in 1177, and it's one of the best-preserved medieval castles in Ireland, surrounded by the sea on three sides. It's also the place the much-loved folk song Carrickfergus is named after

name: Glenarm and the Antrim coast road
name_zh: 格莱纳姆 · 安特里姆海岸公路
note: 萨克雷沿着刚修好的安特里姆海岸公路一路北上，在《爱尔兰札记》里赞叹这段路的风景。今天这条路仍被认为是世界上最美的海岸公路之一
note_en: Thackeray travelled north along the newly built Antrim Coast Road, and in The Irish Sketch Book he raves about the scenery. It's still considered one of the most beautiful coastal drives in the world

name: Whitby
prototype_of: 《西尔维娅的恋人》里蒙克黑文的原型。1859 年盖斯凯尔来惠特比住了一段时间，打听拿破仑战争时期强征水手的“抓壮丁队”在这座捕鲸港里引起的骚乱，把它写成了这部小说
prototype_of_en: Whitby is the model for Monkshaven in Sylvia's Lovers. Elizabeth Gaskell stayed here in 1859 to research the riots that broke out in this whaling port when press gangs came to force local men into the navy during the Napoleonic Wars. That history became her novel

name: Scarborough
prototype_of: 常被认为是《艾格妮丝·格雷》结尾海滨小城的原型。安妮·勃朗特很爱这里，1849 年病重时坚持来看海，几天后死在这里，二十九岁。她葬在圣玛利亚教堂墓园，是勃朗特姐妹中唯一不葬在霍沃斯的
prototype_of_en: Scarborough is often thought to be the seaside town at the end of Agnes Grey. Anne Brontë loved it here. In 1849, when she was dying, she insisted on coming to see the sea one last time, and she died here a few days later, aged twenty-nine. She's buried in St Mary's churchyard, the only one of the Brontë sisters not buried at Haworth

name: Little Town, Newlands Valley
name_zh: 纽兰兹谷 · 小镇农场
note: 《温迪琪·温克太太的故事》里，小女孩露西就住在纽兰兹谷的小镇农场，她去山上找丢失的手帕，遇见了刺猬洗衣妇温迪琪·温克太太。波特常来附近度夏，书里的山坡和小路都照这里画
note_en: In The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle, a little girl named Lucie lives at Little-town farm in the Newlands Valley. While searching the fellside for her lost handkerchiefs, she meets Mrs Tiggy-Winkle, a hedgehog who does everyone's washing. Beatrix Potter spent summers nearby and drew the hills and lanes straight from life

name: Greenheys, Manchester
name_zh: 曼彻斯特 · 格林海斯
note: 《玛丽·巴顿》开篇，曼彻斯特工人们在格林海斯的田野里散步，这是城里人逃离工厂烟尘的地方。小说写成时这里还是田野，后来就被城市吞没了
note_en: Mary Barton opens with Manchester workers strolling through Green Heys Fields, where people went to get away from the smoke of the cotton mills. When Gaskell wrote the novel, these were still open fields. The city swallowed them up long ago

name: The Great White Horse, Ipswich
name_zh: 伊普斯威奇 · 大白马客栈
note: 《匹克威克外传》里最有名的尴尬场面：匹克威克先生半夜在大白马客栈迷宫般的走廊里找不到房间，误闯进一位戴着卷发纸的中年女士的卧室。狄更斯 1835 年当记者时就住过这家客栈
note_en: This is the setting of the most famous embarrassment in The Pickwick Papers. Late at night, lost in the inn's maze of corridors, Mr Pickwick blunders into the wrong bedroom and finds a middle-aged lady in curl-papers getting ready for bed. Dickens had stayed at the Great White Horse himself as a young reporter in 1835

name: Norwich
note: 乔治·博罗在诺里奇长大，《拉文格罗》写的就是他在这里的少年时代：学语言、结识吉普赛人、在城堡山上看风景。他把诺里奇称作“一座美好的老城”
note_en: George Borrow grew up in Norwich, and Lavengro tells the story of his youth here: learning languages, making friends with Romany travellers, and looking out over the city from Castle Hill. 'A fine old city, truly, is that,' he wrote

name: Bala and Llyn Tegid
note: 博罗在《狂野的威尔士》里来到巴拉，赞美泰吉德湖，在镇上的客栈吃了一顿让他念念不忘的早餐。泰吉德湖是威尔士最大的天然湖，传说湖底沉着一座古城
note_en: In Wild Wales, Borrow comes to Bala, admires the lake, Llyn Tegid, and eats a breakfast at the inn that he never stopped talking about. Llyn Tegid is the largest natural lake in Wales, and legend says there's a drowned town at the bottom of it

name: King's Cross Station
note: 九又四分之三站台的所在。哈利推着行李车冲向两个站台之间的砖墙，进入了魔法世界。车站里专门留了一面墙，墙上嵌着半截行李车，旁边是哈利·波特商店。罗琳的父母当年就是在一趟从国王十字车站开出的火车上认识的
note_en: This is home to Platform Nine and Three-Quarters, where Harry pushes his trolley straight at the wall between two platforms and into the wizarding world. The station has set aside a wall with half a luggage trolley disappearing into it, right next to a Harry Potter shop. Fittingly, J. K. Rowling's parents first met on a train leaving King's Cross
coord_checked: London King's Cross railway station - Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_King%27s_Cross_railway_station, 2026-11-03

name: Salisbury
note: 《长日将尽》里管家史蒂文斯开着主人的车第一次出远门，第一晚就停在索尔兹伯里，他在日记里称赞这座大教堂的尖塔。这座尖塔是全英最高的，大教堂里还藏着四份《大宪章》原件之一
note_en: In The Remains of the Day, Stevens takes his employer's car on the first long trip of his life, and he spends his first night in Salisbury, where he admires the cathedral spire. It's the tallest spire in Britain, and the cathedral also holds one of the four surviving original copies of Magna Carta

name: Weymouth Pier
note: 《长日将尽》的结尾：史蒂文斯坐在韦茅斯码头的长椅上，看着码头的灯一盏盏亮起，一个陌生人对他说：“晚上是一天里最好的时候。”他终于开始回想自己错过了什么
note_en: The Remains of the Day ends here. Stevens sits on a bench on Weymouth pier, watching the lights come on, when a stranger tells him that the evening is the best part of the day. For the first time, he begins to face up to everything he has missed

name: St Thomas' Hospital
note: 《赎罪》第三部，十八岁的布里奥妮放弃剑桥，在这家医院当见习护士，在敦刻尔克撤退后涌来的伤兵中赎罪。医院就在议会大厦对岸，南丁格尔的第一所护士学校也开在这里
note_en: In Part Three of Atonement, eighteen-year-old Briony gives up her place at Cambridge to train as a nurse here. She cares for the wounded soldiers flooding in after Dunkirk, trying to make up for what she has done. The hospital sits right across the river from Parliament, and it's where Florence Nightingale opened her first school of nursing
coord_checked: Bronze Statue of Edward VI at North Entrance to Ward Block of North Wing at St Thomas' Hospital - Historic England list entry 1080372 — https://historicengland.org.uk/listing/the-list/list-entry/1080372, 2026-11-03

name: Holy Trinity Church, Clapham Common
name_zh: 克拉珀姆公园 · 圣三一教堂
note: 《赎罪》里，布里奥妮悄悄走进克拉珀姆公园边的圣三一教堂，看着表姐罗拉嫁给了当年真正的施暴者保罗·马歇尔——她这才明白自己的谎言造成了什么。这座教堂也是 19 世纪推动废除奴隶贸易的“克拉珀姆派”的教堂
note_en: In Atonement, Briony slips into Holy Trinity Church on Clapham Common to watch her cousin Lola marry Paul Marshall, the man who really attacked her years before. Only then does Briony fully understand what her lie has done. In the early 1800s the church was home to the Clapham Sect, the group that campaigned to end the slave trade
coord_checked: Church of Holy Trinity, Clapham Town Ward - British Listed Buildings (list entry 1080491) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101080491-church-of-holy-trinity-clapham-town-ward, 2026-11-03

name: Clava Cairns
prototype_of: 常被认为是《古战场传奇》里克雷格纳敦立石圈的灵感来源：克莱尔在这样的古老石圈里触摸巨石，跌回了 1743 年。这片四千年前的墓冢和立石离卡洛登战场只有一英里多
prototype_of_en: These stones are often said to have inspired Craigh na Dun in Outlander, the stone circle where Claire touches a standing stone and finds herself in 1743. The burial cairns and standing stones here are around four thousand years old, and Culloden Battlefield is just over a mile away
coord_checked: MHG4366 - Central ring cairn - Balnuaran of Clava - Highland Historic Environment Record — https://her.highland.gov.uk/Monument/MHG4366, 2026-11-03

name: Paddington Station
note: 一只戴旧帽子、挂着“请照顾这只熊”标签的小熊坐在这里的失物招领处旁，被布朗一家领回了家，于是有了帕丁顿熊。车站里有他的铜像。克里斯蒂的《命案目睹记》也从“4 点 50 分从帕丁顿开出”的列车开始
note_en: A small bear in a battered hat, with a label around his neck that said 'Please look after this bear. Thank you', was sitting near the lost property office here when the Brown family found him and took him home. That's how he got his name. There's a bronze statue of him in the station. Agatha Christie's 4.50 from Paddington also begins on a train leaving from here

name: Marble Arch
note: 老舍《二马》开篇，马威一个人坐在玉石牌楼边的海德公园里，心事重重；故事随后才倒回他和父亲刚到伦敦的时候。这座拱门原本是白金汉宫的大门，后来搬到了这里
note_en: Lao She's Mr Ma and Son opens with young Ma Wei sitting alone in Hyde Park near Marble Arch, lost in thought, before the story jumps back to when he and his father first arrived in London. The arch originally stood at the entrance to Buckingham Palace and was later moved here

name: Dover Street, Mayfair
note: “汤米，老伙计！”“塔彭丝，老朋友！”——《秘密对手》一开头，这对一战后找不到工作的年轻人在多佛街地铁站出口重逢，挡住了出站的人流。他们随后合伙开起“年轻冒险家公司”，成了克里斯蒂笔下的侦探搭档。这座地铁站 1933 年改名为绿园站
note_en: 'Tommy, old thing!' 'Tuppence, old bean!' The Secret Adversary opens with two young friends, both out of work after the war, bumping into each other at the exit of Dover Street Tube station and blocking everyone's way. They go on to start a business called the Young Adventurers and become Agatha Christie's famous detective duo. The station was renamed Green Park in 1933

name: Piccadilly Circus
note: 《秘密对手》里，汤米和塔彭丝在皮卡迪利广场附近相约，决定合伙开一家“年轻冒险家公司”。广场中央俗称“爱神”的雕像其实是基督教慈善之神安忒洛斯
note_en: In The Secret Adversary, Tommy and Tuppence talk over their plans near Piccadilly Circus and decide to go into business together as the Young Adventurers. The statue in the middle that everyone calls Eros is actually his brother Anteros, the god of selfless love

name: Soho
note: 伦敦文学里最暧昧的街区：杰基尔医生给海德先生在苏豪租了住处；《双城记》里马内特医生一家住在苏豪广场旁一个安静的街角，今天那里有条街就叫马内特街；《好兆头》里天使亚茨拉斐尔的旧书店也开在苏豪
note_en: Soho has always had a shady side in London literature. Dr Jekyll rents rooms here for Mr Hyde. In A Tale of Two Cities, Dr Manette and his daughter live in a quiet corner near Soho Square, and there's a street nearby now called Manette Street. And in Good Omens, the angel Aziraphale runs his secondhand bookshop in Soho

name: Holyhead
note: 从伦敦去都柏林的老路就在这里接上渡轮：1848 年起，“爱尔兰邮车”每天从尤斯顿开到霍利黑德。《秘密对手》里，汤米一行为追查失踪的简·芬恩坐火车赶到这里，一路上他的火气也消了。今天渡轮仍开往都柏林，港口旁的圣西比教堂建在罗马时代的堡垒墙里
note_en: This is where the old road from London to Dublin meets the sea: from 1848 the Irish Mail train ran every day from Euston to Holyhead. In The Secret Adversary, Tommy and a companion take the train here on the trail of the missing Jane Finn, and his temper cools a little on the way. Ferries still leave for Dublin, and St Cybi's Church by the harbour stands inside the walls of a Roman fort

name: Torquay
note: 阿加莎·克里斯蒂 1890 年生在托基，在这里长大。一战期间她在镇上医院的药房帮忙，学会了辨认各种毒药，后来就用在了第一部小说《斯泰尔斯庄园奇案》里。镇上有一条串起她生平地点的“阿加莎·克里斯蒂之路”
note_en: Agatha Christie was born in Torquay in 1890 and grew up here. During the First World War she worked in the dispensary of the local hospital, where she learned all about poisons. She put that knowledge to good use in her very first novel, The Mysterious Affair at Styles. Today the town has an Agatha Christie Mile that links places from her life

name: Greenway
note: 克里斯蒂把这座达特河畔的庄园叫作“世界上最可爱的地方”，1938 年起每年夏天来这里度假。她把庄园和河边的船屋写进了《古屋疑云》，船屋就是书里的命案现场。现在由国民信托开放，屋里保留着她一家的收藏
note_en: Christie called Greenway, high above the River Dart, 'the loveliest place in the world', and she spent her summers here from 1938 onwards. She used the house in Dead Man's Folly, where the boathouse down by the river becomes the scene of the murder. The National Trust now runs the house, and it's still full of the family's things

name: St Mary's Church, Cholsey
name_zh: 乔尔西 · 圣玛丽教堂
note: 克里斯蒂 1976 年去世，葬在离她沃灵福德家不远的圣玛利亚教堂墓园，丈夫马克斯·马洛温后来葬在她身旁。墓碑上刻着斯宾塞《仙后》里的诗句：劳作后的安眠、风暴后的港湾
note_en: Agatha Christie died in 1976 and was buried in the churchyard here, not far from her home in Wallingford. Her husband, Max Mallowan, was later buried beside her. Her headstone quotes a line from Spenser's Faerie Queene: 'Sleep after toyle, port after stormie seas'
coord_checked: Church of St Mary, Cholsey (British Listed Buildings, Historic England list entry 1059283) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101059283-church-of-st-mary-cholsey, 2026-11-03

name: Burgh Island
prototype_of: 常被认为是《无人生还》里士兵岛和《阳光下的罪恶》里那座小岛的原型：退潮时能走上岛，涨潮时只能坐高脚“海上拖拉机”过去。克里斯蒂住过岛上的装饰艺术风格酒店，酒店至今营业
prototype_of_en: Burgh Island is often said to have inspired Soldier Island in And Then There Were None and the island in Evil Under the Sun. At low tide you can walk across the sand. At high tide you ride over on the 'sea tractor', a platform on tall stilts. Christie stayed at the island's Art Deco hotel, which is still open

name: Andover
note: 《ABC 谋杀案》的第一起谋杀：凶手按字母顺序作案，A 是安多弗，一位开烟草店的老太太被害，尸体旁放着一本 ABC 铁路时刻表。白罗收到了凶手的挑战信
note_en: The first murder in The ABC Murders happens here. The killer is working through the alphabet, and A is for Andover, where an elderly woman who runs a tobacco shop is found dead with an ABC railway guide lying beside her. Poirot has already received a letter from the killer, daring him to stop it
coord_checked: Andover, Hampshire - Wikipedia (OS grid reference SU3646, converted with osgrid.py, centre of 1 km square) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Hampshire, 2026-11-03

name: Bexhill-on-Sea
note: 《ABC 谋杀案》的 B：一位年轻女侍者在贝克斯希尔的海边被勒死，身旁又是一本 ABC 铁路时刻表。这座安静的海滨小城因此出现在了最有名的侦探小说之一里
note_en: B is for Bexhill in The ABC Murders. A young waitress is found strangled on the seafront, with another ABC railway guide beside her. This quiet seaside town ended up in one of the most famous detective novels ever written
coord_checked: Bexhill-on-Sea - Wikipedia (OS grid reference TQ737092, converted with osgrid.py) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bexhill-on-Sea, 2026-11-03

name: Churston Ferrers
note: 《ABC 谋杀案》的 C：卡迈克尔·克拉克爵士在彻斯顿的家附近遇害。彻斯顿就在克里斯蒂自己的格林威庄园旁边，她把凶案放在了家门口
note_en: C is for Churston in The ABC Murders. Sir Carmichael Clarke is murdered near his home here. Churston is right next door to Greenway, Christie's own holiday house, so she set this murder practically on her doorstep

name: Doncaster
note: 《ABC 谋杀案》的 D：凶手选在圣莱杰赛马日的唐卡斯特下手，满城人潮成了最好的掩护，白罗也在这里揭开了真相。圣莱杰赛始于 1776 年，是英国五大经典赛里最古老的一场
note_en: D is for Doncaster in The ABC Murders. The killer strikes on the day of the St Leger horse race, when the town is packed with people and it's easy to disappear into the crowd, and it's here that Poirot finally begins to see the truth. First run in 1776, the St Leger is the oldest of Britain's five classic horse races
coord_checked: Doncaster - Wikipedia (OS grid reference SE575032, converted with osgrid.py) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doncaster, 2026-11-03

name: St Martin's Theatre
note: 克里斯蒂的《捕鼠器》1952 年首演，1974 年起在这家剧院上演，是世界上连续上演时间最长的戏。每场结束时，演员都会请观众替凶手的身份保密——七十多年来大家一直守着这个约定
note_en: Christie's The Mousetrap opened in 1952 and moved to this theatre in 1974. It's the longest-running play in the world. At the end of every performance, the cast asks the audience not to reveal who the murderer is, and for more than seventy years audiences have kept the secret

name: Lyme Park, Cheshire
scene: 达西先生的彭伯里庄园外景。1995 年 BBC 剧集里科林·费斯穿着湿透的衬衫从湖里走上来、撞见伊丽莎白的那一幕就在这里拍，这个原著里没有的镜头成了英剧史上最有名的画面之一
scene_en: the outside of Pemberley, Mr Darcy's estate. This is where Colin Firth walks out of the lake in a soaking wet shirt and runs into Elizabeth in the 1995 BBC series. The scene isn't in the book at all, but it became one of the most famous moments in British television

name: Castle Howard
scene: 弗莱特家族的布赖兹赫德庄园，查尔斯第一次跟着塞巴斯蒂安走进这座巴洛克宫殿就爱上了它（2008 年电影也在这里拍）。庄园至今由霍华德家族居住，对外开放
scene_en: Brideshead, the Flyte family's house, which Charles falls in love with the first time Sebastian brings him here (it played the same role again in the 2008 film). The Howard family still lives here, and the house is open to visitors

name: The Dark Hedges, County Antrim
name_zh: 安特里姆郡 · 黑暗树篱
scene: 国王大道，艾莉亚逃离君临时走的那条路。两排山毛榉是 18 世纪斯图尔特家族为装点通往庄园的车道种下的，枝条在头顶交缠成拱。如今这条路已经禁止车辆通行，只能步行进去，几场风暴吹倒了好几棵老树，剩下的仍是北爱尔兰最上镜的地方之一
scene_en: the Kingsroad, the road Arya travels when she escapes from King's Landing. The Stuart family planted the two rows of beeches in the eighteenth century to line the drive up to their house, and the branches now meet overhead. The road is closed to cars, so you walk in. Storms have brought down several of the old trees, but it's still one of the most photographed places in Northern Ireland

name: Dylan Thomas Boathouse, Laugharne
name_zh: 拉恩 · 迪伦·托马斯船屋
note: 迪伦·托马斯生命最后四年（1949–1953）的家，《牛奶树下》就是在这里写完的，书里那个海边小镇有不少拉恩的影子。船屋现在是博物馆和茶室，悬崖路上那间俯瞰塔夫河口的写作小棚还保持着他离开时的样子，他就葬在村里的圣马丁教堂墓地
note_en: Dylan Thomas's home for the last four years of his life, 1949 to 1953. He finished Under Milk Wood here, and its seaside town owes a lot to Laugharne. The Boathouse is now a museum with a tea room, his writing shed above the Taf estuary along Cliff Road is kept the way he left it, and he's buried in St Martin's churchyard in the village

name: Abbotsford
note: 司各特用《威弗莱》系列小说的稿费盖起这座城堡式宅第，里面塞满了苏格兰历史文物。1826 年他投资的出版社破产，他背上巨债，拒绝宣告破产，余生拼命写作还债，1832 年在这里去世。宅子和他的藏书楼至今对外开放
note_en: Walter Scott built this castle-like house with the money from his Waverley novels and filled it with relics of Scottish history. In 1826 his publishing business collapsed and left him with enormous debts. He refused to declare bankruptcy and spent the rest of his life writing at a furious pace to pay them off, until he died here in 1832. The house and his library are open to visitors

name: Dr Johnson's House, Gough Square
name_zh: 高夫广场 · 约翰生博士故居
note: 高夫广场 17 号，塞缪尔·约翰生 1748 至 1759 年住在这里，编成了他的《英语词典》；1914 年起成为博物馆
note_en: Samuel Johnson lived at 17 Gough Square from 1748 to 1759, and it was here that he compiled his famous Dictionary of the English Language. The house has been a museum since 1914
coord_checked: Dr Johnson's House (The Great Britain Guide) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/dr-johnsons-house/, 2026-11-04

name: Tottenham Court Road
note: 《死亡圣器》里，比尔和芙蓉的婚礼遭食死徒袭击，赫敏情急之下带着哈利和罗恩幻影移形到了托特纳姆宫路，他们在一家通宵咖啡馆里又被追上。从这里开始，三人踏上了逃亡和寻找魂器的路
note_en: In Deathly Hallows, Death Eaters attack Bill and Fleur's wedding, and Hermione apparates with Harry and Ron to Tottenham Court Road. The Death Eaters track them down again in an all-night café. From here, the three of them go on the run and begin their hunt for Voldemort's Horcruxes

name: Forest of Dean
note: 《死亡圣器》里，三人逃亡时在迪安森林扎营，哈利跟着一头银色的牝鹿守护神找到了冰湖底的格兰芬多宝剑。罗琳在森林边上的塔茨希尔长大，这片森林是她童年的风景
note_en: In Deathly Hallows, Harry, Ron and Hermione camp in the Forest of Dean, and Harry follows a silver doe Patronus to Gryffindor's sword at the bottom of a frozen pool. J. K. Rowling grew up in Tutshill, right on the edge of the forest, so these woods were part of her childhood

name: Gloucester Cathedral cloisters

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

scene: 霍格沃茨的走廊：扇形拱顶的回廊里，墙上出现血字“密室已经被打开”（第一部和第六部电影也在这里拍）。这道 14 世纪回廊的扇形拱顶是英国最早的
scene_en: the corridors of Hogwarts, where the words 'The Chamber of Secrets has been opened' appear written in blood on the cloister wall. The cathedral also appears in the first and sixth films. Its fourteenth-century cloister has the earliest fan vaulting in England

name: Clachaig Gully, Glen Coe
name_zh: 格伦科 · 克拉哈格沟

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

scene: 海格小屋和霍格沃茨场地的布景，搭在格伦科山沟脚下，鹰头马身有翼兽巴克比克就在这里差点被处决。格伦科是苏格兰最壮丽也最悲伤的山谷
scene_en: the set for Hagrid's hut and the Hogwarts grounds, built at the foot of this gully in Glencoe. It's where Buckbeak the hippogriff is almost executed. Glencoe is one of Scotland's most dramatic glens, and one with a tragic history
coord_checked: Clachaig Inn (The Great Britain Guide); the sets stood just north of the inn (Wikipedia, Glen Coe) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/clachaig-inn/, 2026-11-04

name: Steall Falls, Glen Nevis
name_zh: 尼维斯谷 · 斯蒂尔瀑布

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

scene: 三强争霸赛第一个项目里，哈利骑着火弩箭躲避匈牙利树蜂龙时掠过的瀑布。斯蒂尔瀑布落差 120 米，是苏格兰第二高的瀑布，要从尼维斯峡谷徒步进去
scene_en: the waterfall Harry swoops past on his Firebolt while dodging the Hungarian Horntail in the first task of the Triwizard Tournament. Steall Falls drops 120 metres and is often called Scotland's second-highest waterfall. You reach it on foot, through the gorge of Glen Nevis

name: Claremont Square, Islington
name_zh: 伊斯灵顿 · 克莱蒙特广场

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix

scene: 凤凰社总部格里莫广场 12 号：哈利第一次来时，11 号和 13 号之间的那栋房子把两边的房子挤开、凭空冒了出来。电影用的是这排乔治王时代的连排屋
scene_en: 12 Grimmauld Place, headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix. When Harry first arrives, the house squeezes its way into view between numbers 11 and 13. The film used this terrace of Georgian houses

name: Millennium Bridge

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince

scene: 开场食死徒呼啸着穿过伦敦、扭断并摧毁的那座桥。这座通往圣保罗大教堂和泰特现代美术馆的步行桥 2000 年刚开通时摇晃得厉害，被伦敦人戏称为“摇摇桥”
scene_en: the bridge the Death Eaters twist and tear apart as they streak across London in the opening scenes. This footbridge between St Paul's and Tate Modern swayed so badly when it first opened in 2000 that Londoners nicknamed it the Wobbly Bridge

name: Freshwater West, Pembrokeshire
name_zh: 彭布罗克郡 · 弗雷什沃特西海滩

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows

scene: 比尔和芙蓉的贝壳小屋，以及多比的墓：哈利亲手在沙丘上挖坟，石头上写着“这里躺着多比，一个自由的小精灵”。粉丝至今会在这里留下袜子和贝壳，多比的墓被保留了下来
scene_en: Shell Cottage, Bill and Fleur's home, and Dobby's grave, which Harry digs by hand in the sand dunes. The stone reads 'Here lies Dobby, a free elf.' Fans still leave socks and seashells here, and the grave has been allowed to stay

name: Malham Cove

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1

scene: 哈利和赫敏逃亡途中扎营的地方，帐篷搭在石灰岩崖顶那片像铺路石一样的石林上。这道 80 米高的弧形岩壁是一万多年前冰川融水冲出来的
scene_en: the spot where Harry and Hermione pitch their tent while on the run, up on the strange limestone pavement at the top of the cliff. This huge curved cliff, about eighty metres high, was carved out by glacial meltwater more than ten thousand years ago

name: De Vere House, Lavenham
name_zh: 拉文纳姆 · 德维尔宅

adaptation.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1

scene: 戈德里克山谷的背景：哈利出生和父母遇害的地方，用的是德维尔宅。拉文纳姆是英格兰保存最好的中世纪羊毛商小镇，街上满是歪斜的木结构老屋
scene_en: the backdrop for Godric's Hollow, where Harry was born and where his parents died. The filmmakers used De Vere House. Lavenham is the best-preserved medieval wool town in England, and its streets are lined with crooked old timber-framed houses

name: Charing Cross Road
note: 伦敦的书店街。海伦·汉芙和马克斯书店之间二十年的通信让“查令十字路 84 号”成了全世界书迷的地址，原址墙上有纪念牌。朱自清 1931 至 1932 年在伦敦时也常来这里淘书，《伦敦杂记》里专门写了这条街
note_en: Charing Cross Road is London's street of bookshops. The twenty-year correspondence between the New York writer Helene Hanff and the booksellers at Marks & Co made 84 Charing Cross Road famous among book lovers everywhere, and a plaque now marks the spot. The Chinese essayist Zhu Ziqing also spent hours browsing here while living in London in 1931 and 1932, and he wrote about the street in his London Sketches
coord_checked: Foyles (Wikipedia), the shop at 107 Charing Cross Road — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foyles, 2026-11-04

name: Caledonian Park clock tower
note: 朱自清 1931 到 1932 年在伦敦，写过一篇《加尔东尼市场》，记下这个什么旧货都卖的跳蚤市场。市场就开在 1855 年启用的大都会牲畜市场场地上，二战后搬去了伯蒙德赛。当年的钟楼还立在今天的加尔东尼公园里，修复后可以预约爬上去看伦敦
note_en: Zhu Ziqing, who lived in London in 1931 and 1932, wrote an essay about the Caledonian Market, a vast flea market where you could buy just about anything second-hand. It was held on the grounds of the Metropolitan Cattle Market, opened in 1855, and moved to Bermondsey after the Second World War. The market's clock tower still stands in what is now Caledonian Park, and since its restoration you can book a climb to the top for views over London

name: Godstow
prototype_of: 书中没有点名：卡罗尔常带利德尔姐妹划船到戈斯托野餐，1862 年 7 月 4 日那次泛舟途中，他第一次给她们讲了这个故事
prototype_of_en: The book never mentions Godstow, but Carroll often took the Liddell sisters on boat trips and picnics here. It was on one of those trips, on 4 July 1862, that he first told them the story of Alice

name: All Saints' Church, Daresbury
note: 卡罗尔 1832 年生在这里的牧师住宅，父亲当时是这座教堂的牧师；教堂里有 1935 年的纪念彩窗和 2012 年开放的刘易斯·卡罗尔中心
note_en: Lewis Carroll was born at the vicarage here in 1832, when his father was the village curate. The church has a memorial window to him from 1935, and the Lewis Carroll Centre opened beside it in 2012
coord_checked: All Saints Church, Daresbury (The Great Britain Guide) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/all-saints-church-daresbury/, 2026-11-04

name: Lewis Carroll's grave, Guildford
name_zh: 吉尔福德 · 卡罗尔墓
note: 卡罗尔 1898 年在吉尔福德姐妹们的住所“栗树居”去世，葬在山丘公墓，墓上是一座白色大理石十字架。吉尔福德城堡的花园里还有一座爱丽丝穿过镜子的铜像
note_en: Lewis Carroll died in 1898 at The Chestnuts, his sisters' house in Guildford, and was buried here under a simple white marble cross. Down in the gardens of Guildford Castle there's a bronze statue of Alice climbing through the looking-glass
coord_checked: Lewis Carroll's grave, Mount Cemetery (The Tombstone Tourist) — https://thetombstonetourist.com/graves/grave-lewis-carroll-mount-cemetery/, 2026-11-04

name: North Lees Hall, Hathersage
name_zh: 哈瑟塞奇 · 诺斯利斯庄园
prototype_of: 常被认为是桑菲尔德府的原型：1845 年夏洛蒂·勃朗特在哈瑟塞奇的朋友家小住，参观过这座城垛式的庄园宅邸。村里圣米迦勒教堂有艾尔家族的纪念铜像——简·爱的姓很可能就是从这里来的
prototype_of_en: North Lees Hall is often said to be the model for Thornfield Hall in Jane Eyre. In 1845 Charlotte Brontë stayed with a friend in the nearby village of Hathersage and visited this battlemented manor house. In the village church there are old brass memorials to the Eyre family, which may well be where Jane got her surname
coord_checked: North Lees Hall (The Great Britain Guide) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/north-lees-hall/, 2026-11-04

name: Cowan Bridge
prototype_of: 这里的牧师女儿学校是罗沃德的原型，夏洛蒂、艾米莉和两个姐姐玛丽亚、伊丽莎白都在这里上过学；玛丽亚和伊丽莎白离校后不久去世
prototype_of_en: The Clergy Daughters' School here is the model for Lowood in Jane Eyre. Charlotte and Emily Brontë were pupils, along with their older sisters Maria and Elizabeth, who both died after their time at the school

name: Quarry Wood, Cookham Dean
name_zh: 库克姆迪恩 · 采石场林
prototype_of: 《柳林风声》里那片让鼹鼠迷路的野树林，一般认为原型就是这片陡坡上的老林子。格雷厄姆小时候在库克姆迪恩跟外婆住过，后来又搬回这里，在这里把讲给儿子听的故事写成了这本书。林子今天对外开放，小路穿过山毛榉一直下到泰晤士河边
prototype_of_en: The Wild Wood in The Wind in the Willows, where Mole gets lost, is generally thought to be this old wood on a steep slope. Kenneth Grahame lived at Cookham Dean with his grandmother as a boy and came back years later, and it was here that he turned the stories he told his son into the book. The wood is open to walkers today, with paths through the beeches down to the Thames
coord_checked: Quarry Woods walk (Countryfile), grid ref SU886850 — https://www.countryfile.com/go-outdoors/walks/quarry-woods-berkshire, 2026-11-04

name: Kensington Gardens
note: 巴里在这里遇见了卢埃林·戴维斯家的男孩们，每天给他们编故事，彼得·潘就这样诞生了。《肯辛顿公园里的彼得·潘》写的是夜里公园关门后，彼得和仙子、鸟儿在园里生活。长湖边有他的雕像
note_en: J. M. Barrie met the Llewelyn Davies boys here while walking his dog, and made up stories for them every day. That's how Peter Pan was born. Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens tells of Peter living in the park with the fairies and birds after the gates close at night. His statue stands by the Long Water

name: Peter Pan statue, Kensington Gardens
name_zh: 肯辛顿公园 · 彼得·潘雕像
note: 1912 年五一前夜，巴里悄悄让人在长湖边立起这座彼得·潘雕像，第二天一早，孩子们就像发现魔法一样看到了它。雕像立的位置，正是《肯辛顿公园里的彼得·潘》里彼得乘鸟巢船上岸的地方
note_en: On the night before May Day in 1912, J. M. Barrie had this statue put up in secret, so that children walking in the park the next morning would think it had appeared by magic. It stands on the very spot where Peter lands his bird's-nest boat in Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens
coord_checked: Peter Pan statue (The Great Britain Guide) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/peter-pan-statue/, 2026-11-04

name: London Bridge
note: “人群流过伦敦桥，那么多人，我没想到死亡毁了那么多人”——《荒原》里每天早上过桥上班的人群像但丁地狱里的亡魂。艾略特当时就在桥北的劳埃德银行上班，每天也是这人群中的一个
note_en: 'A crowd flowed over London Bridge, so many, / I had not thought death had undone so many.' In The Waste Land, the morning commuters crossing the bridge are like the dead souls in Dante's hell. At the time, T. S. Eliot worked at Lloyds Bank just north of the bridge, so every day he was part of that crowd himself

name: Margate Sands
note: “在马盖特海滩。我能把虚无和虚无连起来。”1921 年艾略特精神崩溃，来马盖特休养，每天坐在海边的避雨亭里写《荒原》。那座亭子如今列为保护建筑，旁边就是特纳当代美术馆
note_en: 'On Margate Sands. / I can connect / Nothing with nothing.' In 1921, after a breakdown, T. S. Eliot came to Margate to recover. He spent his days sitting in a seafront shelter, working on The Waste Land. The shelter is now a listed building, and the Turner Contemporary gallery is just along the front

name: Pudding Lane and the Monument
note: 1666 年 9 月伦敦大火从布丁巷的一家面包房烧起，烧了四天，城里八成以上的房屋被毁。佩皮斯在日记里记下了一切，还把自己的葡萄酒和一块帕尔马奶酪埋进了花园里。大火纪念碑高 202 英尺，正好是它到起火点的距离
note_en: In September 1666, the Great Fire of London broke out in a bakery on Pudding Lane. It burned for four days and destroyed most of the old city. Samuel Pepys recorded it all in his diary, including the moment he buried his wine and a wheel of Parmesan cheese in his garden to save them. The Monument to the fire is 202 feet tall, exactly the distance from its base to where the fire started
coord_checked: Monument to the Great Fire of London (The Great Britain Guide) — https://www.thegreatbritainguide.com/place/monument-to-the-great-fire-of-london/, 2026-11-04

name: Covent Garden
note: 《道林·格雷的画像》里，道林残忍地抛弃了女演员西比尔之后，在黎明时分走过科文特花园的果菜市场，满车的花和水果在晨光里格外鲜艳——回到家，他第一次发现画像的嘴角变了。这里 1974 年以前一直是伦敦最大的果蔬花卉市场
note_en: In The Picture of Dorian Gray, after Dorian cruelly breaks things off with the actress Sibyl Vane, he wanders through Covent Garden market at dawn, among carts piled high with flowers and fruit. When he gets home, he notices for the first time that the mouth in his portrait has changed. Until 1974 this was London's main market for fruit, vegetables and flowers

name: Hardy's Cottage, Higher Bockhampton
name_zh: 上博克汉普顿 · 哈代出生的小屋
note: 哈代 1840 年生在这座他曾祖父盖的茅草顶小屋里，在这里写了《绿林荫下》和《远离尘嚣》；屋旁的荒地和后面的雨冢，被认为是《还乡》里埃格敦荒原的中心。小屋由国民信托管理，可以进去看他写作的小房间，穿过索恩科姆树林就走到荒原
note_en: Thomas Hardy was born in 1840 in this thatched cottage his great-grandfather built, and he wrote Under the Greenwood Tree and Far from the Madding Crowd here. The heath beside it, with Rainbarrow behind, is taken to be the heart of Egdon Heath in The Return of the Native. The National Trust looks after the cottage, so you can see the little room where he wrote, then walk through Thorncombe Wood out onto the heath

name: Aldgate
note: 1665 年伦敦大瘟疫，笛福《瘟疫年纪事》的叙述者住在阿尔德门外，看着圣博托尔夫教堂旁挖下一个巨大的埋尸坑，夜里运尸车一车车把死者倒进去。笛福当时只有五岁，这本书是他几十年后根据记录和回忆写成的
note_en: In Defoe's A Journal of the Plague Year, set during the Great Plague of 1665, the narrator lives just outside Aldgate. He watches a huge pit being dug in the churchyard of St Botolph's and sees the carts tipping in bodies by night. Defoe was only about five years old during the plague. He wrote the book decades later, drawing on records and memories

name: The Heart of Midlothian, Royal Mile
name_zh: 皇家一英里 · 中洛辛郡之心
note: 爱丁堡的老监狱，绰号“中洛辛郡之心”，司各特用它做了小说的书名。监狱 1817 年拆除，皇家一英里路面上用石块拼出的心形标出了它的入口。当地人路过时有朝心上吐口水的老习惯，据说是对监狱的蔑视，也能带来好运
note_en: Edinburgh's old prison was nicknamed the Heart of Midlothian, and Walter Scott used the name as the title of his novel. The prison was demolished in 1817, but a heart shape set into the cobbles of the Royal Mile marks where its entrance stood. Locals still spit on it as they walk past, partly out of contempt for the old jail and partly, they say, for good luck

name: Bedford, site of the county gaol
name_zh: 贝德福德 · 郡监狱旧址
prototype_of: 书中没有点名：做梦人躺下睡觉的“洞穴”通常被理解为贝德福德的监狱；班扬 1660 至 1672 年因传道被关在这里，很可能就是在狱中开始写这本书的
prototype_of_en: The book doesn't name it, but the 'Den' where the dreamer falls asleep is usually read as Bedford gaol. Bunyan was locked up here from 1660 to 1672 for preaching without a licence, and it's probably where he started writing The Pilgrim's Progress
coord_checked: Plaque marking the site of Bedford County Gaol (Geograph photo 1380790, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1380790, 2026-11-04

name: Reform Club, Pall Mall
name_zh: 蓓尔美尔街 · 改革俱乐部
note: 《八十天环游地球》里，福格先生在改革俱乐部和会员们打赌两万英镑，说自己能在八十天内环游地球回到这里。结局他以为自己晚了一天，其实因为一路向东赶上了一天，最后一刻冲进了俱乐部
note_en: In Around the World in Eighty Days, Phileas Fogg bets his fellow members of the Reform Club twenty thousand pounds that he can travel around the globe and be back in this room in eighty days. At the end he thinks he has lost by a single day, until he realises that by travelling east he has actually gained one, and he bursts into the club just in time

name: Whitechapel
note: 1902 年杰克·伦敦穿上破衣服，混在伦敦东区的穷人中间住了几个星期，写成《深渊里的人们》，记录这里的饥饿、拥挤和无家可归。十几年前，开膛手杰克的案子也发生在这片街区
note_en: In 1902 Jack London put on ragged clothes and spent several weeks living among the poorest people of the East End. He wrote about the hunger, the overcrowding and the homelessness he found in The People of the Abyss. About fifteen years earlier, these same streets had been the scene of the Jack the Ripper murders

name: The Elephant House, George IV Bridge
name_zh: 乔治四世桥 · 大象咖啡馆
note: 乔治四世桥 21 号的咖啡馆。罗琳写早期几本《哈利·波特》时常坐在后屋写作，窗外就是爱丁堡城堡。她说过，自己开始写这套书比第一次来这里早好几年，所以这里算不上“诞生地”，但她确实在这里写过。2021 年因火灾停业，2026 年重新开张
note_en: J. K. Rowling used to write in the back room of this café at 21 George IV Bridge, looking out at the castle, while she was working on the early Harry Potter books. She has said she'd already been writing the series for years before she ever came here, so it isn't where Harry was born, but 'I did write in there.' The café closed after a fire in 2021 and reopened in 2026
coord_checked: The Elephant House, 21 George IV Bridge (The Scotsman); the café is across the street from where the Commons photo 'The Elephant House october 2023' was taken (camera 55.94739, -3.19159) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Elephant_House_october_2023.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
note: 老城的墓园，16 世纪末开始使用，罗琳写作期间常来这里散步。墓园里葬着 1806 年去世的托马斯·里德尔和诗人威廉·麦戈纳格尔，常被认为是汤姆·里德尔和麦格教授这两个名字的来源；罗琳说过，里德尔这个名字可能是她无意中记下的
note_en: This Old Town graveyard has been in use since the late 1500s, and Rowling often walked here while she was writing. Among its graves are those of a Thomas Riddell, who died in 1806, and the poet William McGonagall, and many people think that's where the names Tom Riddle and Professor McGonagall came from. Rowling has said she may have picked up the name Riddle here without realising it
coord_checked: Greyfriars Kirkyard (Commons photo 'Greyfriars Kirkyard Memorials', camera location inside the kirkyard 55.9467, -3.19222) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Greyfriars_Kirkyard_Memorials.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Monk's House, Rodmell
name_zh: 罗德梅尔 · 僧舍（伍尔夫故居）
note: 伍尔夫和丈夫伦纳德 1919 年买下的乡间小屋，1940 年起长住；她的许多小说是在花园尽头的写作小屋里成形的。她去世后，伦纳德把她的骨灰葬在花园的榆树下。1980 年起由国民信托作为作家故居开放参观
note_en: Virginia and Leonard Woolf bought this cottage in 1919 and moved here full time in 1940. Many of her novels took shape in the little writing lodge at the bottom of the garden. After her death, Leonard buried her ashes under an elm tree in the garden. The National Trust has run it as a writer's house since 1980
coord_checked: Monk's House, Rodmell (Geograph photo 3940379, subject location; Wikipedia gives 50.8387, 0.0165) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/3940379, 2026-11-04

name: Christ Church, Lewis Carroll's college
name_zh: 牛津 · 卡罗尔任教的基督教堂学院
note: 卡罗尔 1851 年进入基督教堂学院读书，之后留在学院，1855 至 1881 年担任数学讲师；爱丽丝·利德尔是院长亨利·利德尔的女儿。学院大厅里那对长脖子的铜质壁炉柴架，据说给了爱丽丝“脖子越伸越长”的灵感；大厅的彩窗里还有爱丽丝和书中人物
note_en: Lewis Carroll came to Christ Church as a student in 1851 and never really left. He taught mathematics here from 1855 to 1881. Alice Liddell was the daughter of the Dean, Henry Liddell. The long-necked brass firedogs in the college's dining hall are said to have inspired the scene where Alice's neck stretches, and one of the hall's stained-glass windows shows Alice and characters from the book
coord_checked: Mercury fountain at the centre of Tom Quad (Geograph photo 187947, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/187947, 2026-11-04

name: Alice's Shop, St Aldate's
name_zh: 圣奥尔代茨街 · 爱丽丝小店
prototype_of: 《爱丽丝镜中奇遇》第 5 章老羊开的那家小店的原型，坦尼尔的插图画的就是这家店。对面基督教堂学院院长的女儿爱丽丝·利德尔当年常来这里买糖；现在是一家卖爱丽丝纪念品的小店
prototype_of_en: This little shop is the Old Sheep Shop in chapter 5 of Through the Looking-Glass, and Tenniel's illustration shows this very building. Alice Liddell, whose father was Dean of Christ Church just across the road, used to buy sweets here. Today it sells Alice gifts
coord_checked: Alice's Shop, 83 St Aldate's (Geograph photo 8084523, subject location SP 51410 05841) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/8084523, 2026-11-04

name: Talland House, St Ives
name_zh: 圣艾夫斯 · 塔兰德宅
note: 莱斯利·斯蒂芬租下的海边别墅，俯瞰波斯明斯特湾，对岸就是戈德雷维灯塔。伍尔夫出生后的头 13 年，全家每年夏天都在这里住三个月；1894 年以后再没回来。这些夏天后来写进了《到灯塔去》
note_en: Leslie Stephen rented this house above Porthminster Bay for his family's summer holidays, and from its windows you could see Godrevy Lighthouse across the bay. Virginia spent three months here every summer for the first thirteen years of her life, until the family stopped coming after 1894. Those summers are the heart of To the Lighthouse
coord_checked: Talland House (Commons photo 'Talland House, St Ives, Cornwall - May 2022', camera location 50.20842, -5.47912) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Talland_House,_St_Ives,_Cornwall_-_May_2022.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: 46 Gordon Square, Bloomsbury
name_zh: 布卢姆斯伯里 · 戈登广场 46 号
note: 1904 年父亲去世后，斯蒂芬家的兄妹从肯辛顿搬进这栋房子。弗吉尼亚和姐姐瓦妮莎在这里办“周四晚会”，招待哥哥索比的剑桥朋友，这里成了布卢姆斯伯里文化圈最早的聚会地。瓦妮莎结婚后，弗吉尼亚搬去了菲茨罗伊广场；后来凯恩斯住在这里
note_en: After their father died in 1904, the Stephen children moved out of Kensington and into this house. Virginia and her sister Vanessa began hosting 'Thursday Evenings' here for their brother Thoby's friends from Cambridge, and those evenings made the house the first home of the Bloomsbury Group. Virginia moved to Fitzroy Square after Vanessa got married, and the economist John Maynard Keynes later lived here
coord_checked: 46 Gordon Square (Commons photo '46 Gordon Square Bloomsbury Camden London, WC1H 0PD', taken in front of the house, camera location 51.52442, -0.13018) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:46_Gordon_Square_Bloomsbury_Camden_London,_WC1H_0PD.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Hogarth House, Richmond
note: 伍尔夫夫妇 1915 至 1924 年住在这里；1917 年在餐厅的桌子上办起了出版社，以这座房子命名为霍加斯出版社。门口的蓝牌记着这两件事
note_en: Leonard and Virginia Woolf lived here from 1915 to 1924. In 1917 they set up a small printing press on the dining-room table and named it the Hogarth Press, after the house. A blue plaque marks both
coord_checked: Hogarth House, 34 Paradise Road (English Heritage blue plaques); position from the Commons photo 'LEONARD and VIRGINIA WOOLF - Hogarth House 34 Paradise Road Richmond TW9 1SE', camera location 51.460448, -0.300786 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:LEONARD_and_VIRGINIA_WOOLF_-_Hogarth_House_34_Paradise_Road_Richmond_TW9_1SE.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Godrevy Lighthouse
prototype_of: 圣艾夫斯湾小岛上的灯塔，斯蒂芬家的孩子们在塔兰德宅就能望见它。小说把拉姆齐一家搬到了斯凯岛，但书里的灯塔通常被认为来自戈德雷维
prototype_of_en: This is the lighthouse on its little rock in St Ives Bay that the Stephen children used to gaze at from Talland House. In To the Lighthouse, Woolf moves the Ramsay family to the Isle of Skye, but the lighthouse in the novel is usually traced back to Godrevy
coord_checked: Godrevy Lighthouse, Godrevy Island (Geograph photo 407138, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/407138, 2026-11-04

name: Senate House, University of London
name_zh: 伦敦大学 · 参议院大楼
prototype_of: 常被认为是“真理部”的原型：二战期间这里是英国新闻部所在地，奥威尔的妻子艾琳就在新闻部的审查处工作。这座装饰艺术风格的大楼建于 1932 至 1937 年
