prototype_of_en: Senate House is usually taken to be the model for the Ministry of Truth in 1984. During the Second World War it housed the Ministry of Information, where Orwell's wife, Eileen, worked in the censorship department. The Art Deco tower was built between 1932 and 1937

name: Barnhill, Isle of Jura
name_zh: 朱拉岛 · 巴恩希尔农舍
note: 朱拉岛北部的农舍，奥威尔 1946 年至 1949 年 1 月断断续续住在这里，在这里写完了《一九八四》。现在仍作度假屋出租，屋子基本保持他住时的样子
note_en: Orwell lived on and off at this remote farmhouse in the north of Jura from 1946 to January 1949, and it was here that he finished 1984. It's still rented out to holidaymakers, and it's not much changed since he left

name: George Orwell's grave, Sutton Courtenay
name_zh: 萨顿考特尼 · 奥威尔墓
note: 奥威尔以本名埃里克·亚瑟·布莱尔葬在诸圣堂的墓园。他希望葬在英格兰乡间的教堂墓地，大卫·阿斯特的家族是这里的庄园主，由他安排了这块墓地
note_en: Orwell is buried in All Saints' churchyard under his real name, Eric Arthur Blair. He wanted to lie in an ordinary English country churchyard, and his friend David Astor, whose family owned the local manor, arranged for him to be buried here
coord_checked: Graves of Astor and Orwell, All Saints, Sutton Courtenay (Geograph photo 362296, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/362296, 2026-11-04

name: Wallington, Hertfordshire
name_zh: 赫特福德郡 · 沃灵顿村
prototype_of: 奥威尔 1936 至 1940 年住在村里基茨巷 2 号的“杂货铺”，开小店、养山羊，也在村里的教堂和艾琳结婚。村里的庄园农场和大谷仓被认为是《动物农场》里那座农场的原型
prototype_of_en: Orwell lived at The Stores, 2 Kits Lane, from 1936 to 1940, where he ran a little village shop and kept goats. He married Eileen in the parish church here. The village's Manor Farm and Great Barn are thought to be the models for the farm in Animal Farm
coord_checked: George Orwell's plaque, Wallington (Geograph photo 6849927, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/6849927, 2026-11-04

name: Barnet
note: 《雾都孤儿》里，奥利弗逃出济贫院，步行七天来到伦敦北边的巴尼特，又累又饿，坐在门阶上时遇见了一个奇怪的少年“机灵鬼”，从此被带进了费金的贼窝
note_en: In Oliver Twist, Oliver runs away and walks for seven days until he reaches Barnet, on the edge of London. Exhausted and starving, he's sitting on a doorstep when a strange boy called the Artful Dodger comes along and leads him to Fagin's den of thieves
coord_checked: Barnet High Street (Geograph photo 369802, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/369802, 2026-11-04

name: Cornhill
note: 斯克鲁吉的账房就在康希尔一带。《圣诞颂歌》里，可怜的小职员鲍勃·克拉奇特下班后，在康希尔街上跟一群孩子排队滑冰道，一连滑了二十次，“为了庆祝圣诞夜”
note_en: Scrooge's counting-house is in this part of the City. In A Christmas Carol, once poor Bob Cratchit is finally let off work, he joins a line of boys sliding on the ice on Cornhill and goes down the slide twenty times 'in honour of its being Christmas Eve'
coord_checked: St Peter upon Cornhill, Cornhill (Geograph photo 1767459, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1767459, 2026-11-04

name: Orkney
note: 《弗兰肯斯坦》里，维克多答应怪物再造一个伴侣，躲到奥克尼群岛最偏远的一座小岛上工作，却在快完成时亲手毁了她，怪物在窗外看着，发誓要在他的新婚之夜报复
note_en: In Frankenstein, Victor agrees to build a mate for his creature and goes off to work in secret on one of the most remote islands in Orkney. Just before he finishes, he tears her apart, while the creature watches through the window and swears to get revenge on Victor's wedding night
coord_checked: Kirkwall, Orkney Mainland (Geograph photo 5726878, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/5726878, 2026-11-04

name: Exeter
note: 《理智与情感》里达什伍德母女失去家产后，搬到埃克塞特以北四英里的巴顿小屋。玛丽安在附近山上扭伤脚踝，被英俊的威洛比抱回家，故事由此展开
note_en: In Sense and Sensibility, after the Dashwood women lose their family home, they move to Barton Cottage, four miles north of Exeter. When Marianne twists her ankle on a nearby hill, the handsome Willoughby carries her home, and the story really gets going
coord_checked: Exeter Cathedral (Commons photo 'Exeter (Devon, UK), Cathedral Church of Saint Peter -- 2013 -- 1417', object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Exeter_(Devon,_UK),_Cathedral_Church_of_Saint_Peter_--_2013_--_1417.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Bristol harbour
note: 《金银岛》里，乡绅特里劳尼在布里斯托尔港装备“伊斯班袅拉号”，独腿的西尔弗就在码头边开着“望远镜”酒馆。港口边的老酒馆兰多格驳船据说启发了史蒂文森
note_en: In Treasure Island, Squire Trelawney fits out the Hispaniola in Bristol harbour, and Long John Silver runs the Spy-glass tavern down by the docks. The Llandoger Trow, an old pub on the harbourside, is said to have inspired Stevenson
coord_checked: Floating Harbour, Bristol (Geograph photo 1858154, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1858154, 2026-11-04

name: Portland Place
note: 《三十九级台阶》的开端：理查德·汉内回到波特兰坊附近的公寓，一个陌生人敲门说自己掌握了一个国际阴谋，几天后就被人杀死在他的屋里。汉内从此开始逃亡
note_en: The Thirty-Nine Steps begins here. Richard Hannay gets back to his flat near Portland Place, and a stranger knocks on his door with a story about an international conspiracy. A few days later the man is found murdered in Hannay's flat, and Hannay has to go on the run
coord_checked: Portland Place, Central London (Geograph photo 4675256, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/4675256, 2026-11-04

name: York
note: “我 1632 年生在约克城一个好人家”——《鲁滨逊漂流记》的第一句就把他的家乡放在这里。他违背父亲的意愿出海，从此再没有回来过那种安稳的中产生活
note_en: 'I was born in the year 1632, in the city of York, of a good family.' That's the very first line of Robinson Crusoe. Crusoe runs off to sea against his father's wishes and never returns to the comfortable middle-class life he was born into
coord_checked: York Minster (Commons photo 'York Minster Nave 2, Nth Yorkshire, UK - Diliff', camera location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:York_Minster_Nave_2,_Nth_Yorkshire,_UK_-_Diliff.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Emmanuel College, Cambridge
name_zh: 剑桥 · 伊曼纽尔学院
note: 《格列佛游记》开头，格列佛自我介绍说十四岁进了剑桥伊曼纽尔学院，读了三年，因为家里供不起才去学医、出海。斯威夫特给他一个踏实可信的出身，好让后面的奇遇显得更真
note_en: At the start of Gulliver's Travels, Gulliver tells us he was sent to Emmanuel College, Cambridge, at fourteen and stayed for three years, until his family ran out of money and he trained as a ship's surgeon instead. Swift gives him a solid, believable background so that the wonders that follow seem all the more real
coord_checked: Emmanuel College (Commons photo 'Emmanuel College Front Court, Cambridge, UK - Diliff', camera location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Emmanuel_College_Front_Court,_Cambridge,_UK_-_Diliff.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: Coventry
prototype_of: 很可能是米德尔马契的原型：乔治·艾略特 1841 年随父亲搬到考文垂，在这里住了八年，结识了改变她思想的朋友圈；这座城和小说里的小镇一样靠丝带业为生。她在福尔斯希尔路住过的伯德格罗夫还在，市中心有被炸毁的老大教堂废墟
prototype_of_en: Coventry is probably the model for Middlemarch. George Eliot moved here with her father in 1841 and stayed eight years, falling in with the circle of freethinking friends who changed her outlook, and like the town in the novel, Coventry lived off the silk-ribbon trade. Bird Grove, her house on the Foleshill Road, still stands, and the ruins of the old bombed cathedral are in the city centre
coord_checked: Two spires, Coventry (Geograph photo 1065743, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1065743, 2026-11-04

name: Dorchester
prototype_of: 哈代笔下卡斯特桥的原型：他在附近出生，在多切斯特上学、当建筑学徒，晚年住在城边自己设计的马克斯门。《卡斯特桥市长》整本书就发生在这里，《远离尘嚣》里的人物也来这里赶集。城里有他的雕像和多塞特博物馆里重建的书房
prototype_of_en: Dorchester is the model for Thomas Hardy's Casterbridge. Hardy was born just outside town, went to school and trained as an architect here, and spent his last years at Max Gate, the house he designed on the edge of town. The Mayor of Casterbridge is set entirely in Dorchester, and the characters in Far from the Madding Crowd come here for the market. There's a statue of Hardy in town, and his study has been recreated in the Dorset Museum
coord_checked: Dorchester, View of High West Street (Geograph photo 1834521, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1834521, 2026-11-04

name: Great Maytham Hall, Rolvenden
name_zh: 罗尔文登 · 大梅瑟姆庄园
prototype_of: 伯内特 1898 至 1907 年住在这里，发现庄园里建于 1721 年的围墙花园荒废多年、杂草丛生；《秘密花园》就由此而来
prototype_of_en: Frances Hodgson Burnett lived here from 1898 to 1907. When she arrived she found the old walled garden, built in 1721, overgrown and neglected, and it became the inspiration for The Secret Garden
coord_checked: Great Maytham Hall Garden (Geograph photo 228928, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/228928, 2026-11-04

name: Poohsticks Bridge, Ashdown Forest
name_zh: 阿什当森林 · 噗噗棍桥
prototype_of: 米尔恩常带儿子克里斯托弗·罗宾在阿什当森林散步，这里就是故事里的森林，林中的“五百英亩林”就是“百亩林”。森林外缘哈特菲尔德附近的这座小木桥，就是维尼和朋友们玩“噗噗棍”的地方：从桥上一侧扔下树枝，跑到另一侧看谁的先漂出来。至今游客还在这里玩
prototype_of_en: A. A. Milne often walked in Ashdown Forest with his son, Christopher Robin, and it became the forest in the Winnie-the-Pooh stories. Its Five Hundred Acre Wood is the Hundred Acre Wood. This little wooden bridge near Hartfield is where Pooh and his friends invent the game of Poohsticks: drop sticks off one side, then run to the other side to see whose comes out first. Visitors still play it here today

name: Menabilly and Polridmouth, near Fowey
name_zh: 福伊附近 · 梅纳比利
prototype_of: 杜穆里埃少女时代发现了这座藏在林中的宅子，后来在这里一直住到 1969 年；它和剑桥郡的米尔顿庄园一起成了曼陀丽的原型——曼陀丽也像它一样藏在树林里，从海边看不见。宅子是私产，照片拍的是宅子下面的波利德茅斯小海湾
prototype_of_en: Daphne du Maurier first stumbled on this hidden house as a teenager, and later she lived in it until 1969. Together with Milton Hall in Cambridgeshire, it was the model for Manderley in Rebecca, which, like Menabilly, lies hidden in the woods out of sight of the sea. The house is private. The photo shows Polridmouth Cove just below it

name: Sarehole Mill, Birmingham
name_zh: 伯明翰 · 萨尔霍尔磨坊
prototype_of: 托尔金四到八岁住在这座水磨坊几百码外，他说霍比屯的磨坊就是照它写的，还把这一带的乡野称作“一种失落的乐园”。磨坊今天是博物馆，水车修复后还能转，附近的莫斯利沼泽据说是老林子的灵感来源，沿着步道就能走到
prototype_of_en: From the age of four to eight, Tolkien lived a few hundred yards from this watermill, and he said it was the model for the mill at Hobbiton. He called the countryside here 'a kind of lost paradise'. The mill is a museum now, with its waterwheel restored and turning, and a footpath leads to nearby Moseley Bog, which is said to have inspired the Old Forest

name: Rostrevor and Carlingford Lough
name_zh: 罗斯特雷沃与卡林福德湾
prototype_of: 刘易斯在给哥哥的信里写道，罗斯特雷沃俯瞰卡林福德湾的那一带，就是他心中的纳尼亚；他在贝尔法斯特长大，也提到过这里背后的莫恩山
prototype_of_en: C. S. Lewis once wrote to his brother that the part of Rostrevor looking out over Carlingford Lough was his idea of Narnia. He grew up in Belfast and also named the Mourne Mountains, which rise above the village
coord_checked: Rostrevor and Carlingford Lough (Geograph photo 687576, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/687576, 2026-11-04

name: Hill Top, Near Sawrey
note: 比阿特丽克斯·波特用《彼得兔》的版税在 1905 年买下这座农舍，后来好几本书的插图就画的是这里的房间、花园和村道，汤姆小猫、鸭子杰迈玛都住在这里。她晚年把四千英亩湖区土地留给了国民信托，农舍按她生前的样子保留
note_en: Beatrix Potter bought this farmhouse in 1905 with the money from The Tale of Peter Rabbit. Its rooms, garden and lanes appear in the pictures of several of her books; Tom Kitten and Jemima Puddle-Duck both live here. She later left four thousand acres of the Lake District to the National Trust, and the house has been kept just as she left it

name: Burns Cottage, Alloway
note: 彭斯的父亲 1757 年盖的茅草屋。罗伯特 1759 年 1 月 25 日生在这里，住到七岁左右；现在是苏格兰国民信托管理的罗伯特·彭斯出生地博物馆的一部分
note_en: Robert Burns's father built this thatched cottage in 1757, and Robert was born here on 25 January 1759. He lived here until he was about seven. It's now part of the Robert Burns Birthplace Museum, run by the National Trust for Scotland
coord_checked: Burns Cottage, Alloway (Geograph photo 428032, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/428032, 2026-11-04

name: The Writers' Museum, Lady Stair's House
name_zh: 爱丁堡 · 作家博物馆（莱迪·斯泰尔宅）
note: 皇家一英里旁小巷里这座 1622 年的老宅，专门纪念苏格兰的三位大作家彭斯、司各特和史蒂文森。馆里有彭斯的写字台、印过司各特小说的印刷机，还有史蒂文森房里那只布罗迪执事做的柜子，据说给了《化身博士》灵感。院子的石板上刻着苏格兰作家的名句
note_en: Tucked down a close off the Royal Mile in a house built in 1622, this museum is devoted to Scotland's three great writers, Burns, Scott and Stevenson. You can see Burns's writing desk, the press that printed Scott's novels, and a cabinet made by Deacon Brodie that stood in Stevenson's bedroom and is said to have helped inspire Jekyll and Hyde. Quotations from Scottish writers are carved into the flagstones of the courtyard outside
coord_checked: Lady Stair's House (Geograph photo 2140534, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/2140534, 2026-11-04

name: Elizabeth Gaskell's House, Manchester
name_zh: 曼彻斯特 · 盖斯凯尔故居
note: 盖斯凯尔一家 1850 年搬进普利茅斯林荫路 84 号，她后来的书，包括《克兰福德》和《南方与北方》，都是在这里写的；夏洛蒂·勃朗特来住过三次，狄更斯也来拜访过。2014 年修复后对外开放
note_en: The Gaskells moved into 84 Plymouth Grove in 1850, and Elizabeth wrote all her later books here, including Cranford and North and South. Charlotte Brontë came to stay three times, and Dickens dropped by too. The house was restored and opened to visitors in 2014
coord_checked: Elizabeth Gaskell's House, Plymouth Grove (Geograph photo 720377, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/720377, 2026-11-04

name: D. H. Lawrence Birthplace Museum, Eastwood
name_zh: 伊斯特伍德 · D. H. 劳伦斯出生地博物馆
note: 劳伦斯 1885 年生在维多利亚街 8a 号这座矿工小屋里，伊斯特伍德就是《儿子与情人》里的贝斯特伍德，他父亲在附近的矿井下井。屋子按当年一家人住时的样子布置，还陈列着他最初的墓碑；镇上有步道串起他小说里写到的街道和房子
note_en: D. H. Lawrence was born in this little miner's house at 8a Victoria Street in 1885. Eastwood is the Bestwood of Sons and Lovers, and his father worked down the local pits. The house has been set up the way it would have looked when the family lived here, his original gravestone is on display, and a trail around town links the streets and houses that turn up in his novels
coord_checked: D H Lawrence Birthplace Museum, Eastwood (Geograph photo 7641153, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/7641153, 2026-11-04

name: George Eliot's grave, Highgate Cemetery
name_zh: 海格特公墓 · 乔治·艾略特墓
note: 因为和有妇之夫刘易斯同居多年，乔治·艾略特死后没能葬进威斯敏斯特教堂，诗人角里她的纪念石到 1980 年才放进去。她就葬在海格特东园刘易斯的旁边，墓碑上刻着笔名和婚后的名字玛丽·安·克罗斯，离马克思墓只有几步
note_en: Because she had lived for years with George Henry Lewes, a married man, George Eliot was refused burial in Westminster Abbey, and her memorial stone in Poets' Corner wasn't added until 1980. She lies in Highgate's East Cemetery next to Lewes, under a headstone with both her pen name and her married name, Mary Ann Cross, a few steps from Karl Marx
coord_checked: The grave of George Eliot in Highgate Cemetery (Geograph photo 5876589, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/5876589, 2026-11-04

name: Reading Gaol
note: 王尔德 1895 至 1897 年在这里服刑，编号 C.3.3。他在狱中写下给道格拉斯的长信《自深深处》，出狱后又以亲眼见到的一次绞刑写成《雷丁监狱之歌》，署名就是他的囚号。监狱 2014 年关闭，2021 年外墙上出现了一幅班克西的壁画
note_en: Oscar Wilde was imprisoned here from 1895 to 1897, known only as prisoner C.3.3. In his cell he wrote the long letter later published as De Profundis. After his release he wrote The Ballad of Reading Gaol, about a hanging he had witnessed here, and published it under his prison number. The prison closed in 2014, and in 2021 a Banksy mural appeared on its outer wall

name: J. R. R. Tolkien's grave, Wolvercote Cemetery
name_zh: 牛津沃尔弗科特公墓 · 托尔金墓
note: 托尔金 1973 年去世，和妻子伊迪丝合葬在沃尔弗科特公墓的天主教墓区。墓碑上，他在两人名字下面各刻了一个名字：贝伦和露西恩，他传说里为爱闯过冥府的那对恋人。墓前常摆着世界各地读者留下的花、信和小物件
note_en: Tolkien died in 1973 and is buried with his wife, Edith, in the Catholic section of Wolvercote Cemetery. Under their names on the headstone he added two more, Beren and Lúthien, the lovers from his legends who defied death itself. Readers from all over the world leave flowers, letters and little tributes at the grave
coord_checked: Grave of Edith and J.R.R. Tolkien (Commons photo, camera location at the grave) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Grave_of_Edith_and_J.R.R._Tolkien_in_the_Wolvercote_Cemetery,_Oxonmoot_1979.jpg, 2026-11-04

name: The Kilns, Headington
note: 刘易斯 1930 年和哥哥沃伦、简妮·摩尔一起买下这座房子，此后一直住在这里，纳尼亚系列也是在这里写的；现在是 C. S. 刘易斯基金会的研究中心
note_en: C. S. Lewis bought this house in 1930, together with his brother Warren and Janie Moore, and lived here for the rest of his life. He wrote the Narnia books here. It's now a study centre run by the C. S. Lewis Foundation
coord_checked: The Kilns, home of C.S. Lewis (Geograph photo 7925307, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/7925307, 2026-11-04

name: Bunhill Fields
note: 1665 至 1854 年间不信国教者的墓地，现在是公共花园。布莱克、笛福和班扬都葬在这里：笛福的方尖碑立于 1870 年，班扬的墓上有他的卧像，标出布莱克墓穴位置的石碑 2018 年揭幕
note_en: From 1665 to 1854, this was the burial ground for Londoners who didn't belong to the Church of England. It's now a public garden. William Blake, Daniel Defoe and John Bunyan are all buried here. Defoe's obelisk was put up in 1870, Bunyan's tomb has a carved figure of him lying on top, and a stone marking Blake's grave was unveiled in 2018
coord_checked: Defoe and Blake memorials, Bunhill Fields (Geograph photo 3710090, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/3710090, 2026-11-04

name: St Olave's Church, Hart Street
name_zh: 哈特街 · 圣奥拉夫教堂
note: 佩皮斯所属的教区教堂，日记里称它“我们自己的教堂”。他在这里修了一条从海军部直通的楼廊，1669 年妻子伊丽莎白去世后在这里立了她的胸像，1703 年葬在她身旁
note_en: This was Samuel Pepys's parish church, which he calls 'our own church' in his diary. He had a private gallery built here that he could reach straight from the Navy Office, put up a bust of his wife Elizabeth after she died in 1669, and was buried beside her in 1703
coord_checked: St Olave, Hart Street (Geograph photo 1085120, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1085120, 2026-11-04

name: Mary Shelley's grave, Bournemouth
name_zh: 伯恩茅斯 · 玛丽·雪莱墓
note: 玛丽·雪莱葬在圣彼得教堂的墓园，据说和珀西·比希·雪莱的心脏葬在一起；她的儿子把她的父母玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特和威廉·葛德文也迁葬到这里
note_en: Mary Shelley is buried in St Peter's churchyard, supposedly along with the heart of her husband, Percy Bysshe Shelley. Her son also had her parents, Mary Wollstonecraft and William Godwin, moved here and buried beside her
coord_checked: Grave of Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley (Geograph photo 1861397, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1861397, 2026-11-04

name: Newstead Abbey
note: 拜伦家族的祖宅。1798 年他十岁时连同爵位一起继承下来，1808 年起断断续续住过几段时间，1818 年人在意大利时把它卖掉。《唐璜》第十三到十六章里的诺曼修道院就是照它写的。现在归诺丁汉市政府所有，对外开放，里面有拜伦博物馆
note_en: Newstead was Byron's family home. He inherited it, along with his title, in 1798, when he was ten. He lived here on and off from 1808 and sold it in 1818 while he was in Italy. The Norman Abbey in cantos 13 to 16 of Don Juan is based on it. It now belongs to Nottingham City Council and is open to visitors, with a Byron museum inside

name: Byron's grave, Hucknall
note: 拜伦 1824 年死在希腊的迈索隆吉翁。威斯敏斯特教堂拒绝让他入葬，他被葬进这座圣玛利亚·抹大拉教堂里的拜伦家族墓穴。墓上那块大理石板是希腊国王送的，他的女儿艾达·洛芙莱斯后来也葬在他身旁。威斯敏斯特教堂直到 1969 年才为他立了纪念碑
note_en: Byron died at Missolonghi in Greece in 1824. Westminster Abbey refused to bury him, so he was laid to rest in the family vault here at St Mary Magdalene's. A marble slab sent by the King of Greece covers the grave, and his daughter, Ada Lovelace, was later buried beside him. Westminster Abbey finally put up a memorial to him in 1969
coord_checked: Church of St Mary Magdalene, Hucknall (Wikipedia) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St_Mary_Magdalene,_Hucknall, 2026-11-05

name: St Mary's churchyard, Harrow on the Hill
name_zh: 哈罗山 · 圣玛利亚教堂墓园
note: 拜伦 1801 至 1805 年在哈罗公学读书，常坐在这里的皮奇墓旁发呆，说它是“我最喜欢的墓碑”。诗里那棵榆树 1935 年以前就烧毁了；墓前有一块 1905 年立的石碑，刻着这首诗。他的女儿阿莱格拉葬在教堂南门廊旁，墓上没有标记
note_en: When Byron was a pupil at Harrow School, from 1801 to 1805, he liked to sit and daydream by the Peachey Tomb, which he called his 'favourite tombstone'. The elm tree from his poem had burned down by 1935, but a stone placed in front of the tomb in 1905 has the poem carved on it. His daughter Allegra lies in an unmarked grave by the church's south porch
coord_checked: The Peachey tomb in St Mary's Churchyard, Harrow on the Hill (Geograph photo by Marathon, Commons object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Peachey_tomb_in_St_Mary%27s_Churchyard,_Harrow_on_the_Hill_-_geograph.org.uk_-_4730479.jpg, 2026-11-05

name: Lochnagar
note: 凯恩戈姆山区巴尔莫勒尔庄园里的一座山，海拔 1155 米。拜伦童年有一段时间住在阿伯丁郡，他在这首诗的注里说，自己小时候就住在这座山附近。他在诗里说，宁可要“黑暗的洛赫纳加”荒凉的峭壁，也不要英格兰平和的风景
note_en: Lochnagar is a 1,155-metre mountain on the Balmoral estate in the Cairngorms. Byron spent part of his childhood in Aberdeenshire, and in a note to his poem he says he lived near the mountain as a boy. In the poem he says he'd rather have the wild crags of 'dark Lochnagar' than all of England's gentler scenery

name: Shelley Memorial, University College, Oxford
name_zh: 牛津大学学院 · 雪莱纪念像
note: 雪莱 1810 年进大学学院，1811 年 3 月 25 日因为小册子《无神论的必要性》和朋友霍格一起被开除。现在学院以他为荣：爱德华·昂斯洛·福特雕的溺水诗人大理石像，原本打算放在他罗马的墓地，1893 年起安放在高街边一间带穹顶的小屋里
note_en: Shelley came to University College in 1810 and was thrown out on 25 March 1811, along with his friend Thomas Jefferson Hogg, for writing a pamphlet called The Necessity of Atheism. Today the college honours him. Edward Onslow Ford's marble statue of the drowned poet, which was first meant for his grave in Rome, has stood in a domed room just off the High Street since 1893

name: Albion House, Marlow
note: 雪莱一家 1817 年 3 月到 1818 年 2 月住在西街 104 号的阿尔比恩宅。珀西在马洛附近的树林里写了长诗《莱昂与茜丝娜》（后改名《伊斯兰的起义》），玛丽在这里写完了《弗兰肯斯坦》。房子现在叫雪莱小屋，是私宅，门外有纪念牌
note_en: Percy and Mary Shelley lived at Albion House, 104 West Street, from March 1817 to February 1818. Percy wrote Laon and Cythna, later reissued as The Revolt of Islam, in the woods around Marlow, and Mary finished Frankenstein here. The house is now private, divided into Shelley Cottages, with a plaque outside
coord_checked: Albion House / Shelley Cottage, Marlow (British Listed Buildings, Grade II) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101217597-albion-houseshelley-cottageshelley-house-marlow, 2026-11-05

name: St Peter's Field (Peterloo), Manchester
name_zh: 曼彻斯特 · 圣彼得广场（彼得卢）
note: 1819 年 8 月 16 日，数万人在这里集会要求议会改革，骑兵冲进人群，造成 18 人死亡、数百人受伤。远在意大利的雪莱听到消息，写下《暴政的假面游行》，直到 1832 年才得以出版。这片空地如今是圣彼得广场，旁边立着 2019 年落成的彼得卢纪念碑
note_en: On 16 August 1819, tens of thousands of people gathered here to demand political reform, and cavalry charged into the crowd, killing eighteen and injuring hundreds. Shelley heard the news in Italy and wrote The Mask of Anarchy, which couldn't be published until 1832. The field is now St Peter's Square, and the Peterloo Memorial, unveiled in 2019, stands beside it

name: Milton's Cottage, Chalfont St Giles
name_zh: 查尔芬特圣贾尔斯 · 弥尔顿小屋
note: 1665 年弥尔顿和妻子为躲避伦敦的瘟疫搬进这座小屋，他在这里写完了《失乐园》。1887 年靠公众募捐买下，底层是博物馆，花园对外开放
note_en: Milton and his wife moved into this cottage in 1665 to get away from the plague in London, and he finished Paradise Lost here. It was bought by public subscription in 1887. The ground floor is now a museum, and the garden is open to visitors
coord_checked: Milton's Cottage, Chalfont St. Giles (Geograph photo 8063115, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/8063115, 2026-11-05

name: Coleridge Cottage, Nether Stowey
name_zh: 下斯托伊 · 柯勒律治小屋
note: 柯勒律治 1797 至 1799 年租住在这里，写了《这菩提树荫是我的牢房》《古舟子咏》《午夜寒霜》和《克丽斯塔贝尔》的一部分。1909 年起由国民信托管理
note_en: Coleridge rented this cottage from 1797 to 1799, and in that short time he wrote This Lime-Tree Bower My Prison, The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, Frost at Midnight and part of Christabel. The National Trust has looked after it since 1909

name: Porlock
note: 埃克斯穆尔海岸边的村庄。柯勒律治在《忽必烈汗》的序言里说，1797 年他在波洛克和林顿之间一座僻静的农舍里梦到这首诗，一般认为那座农舍在卡尔伯恩教堂附近；醒来写到一半，“一位从波洛克来办事的人”上门，其余的诗句就都忘了
note_en: Porlock is a village on the Exmoor coast. In his preface to Kubla Khan, Coleridge says he dreamed the whole poem in 1797 at a lonely farmhouse between Porlock and Linton, usually thought to be near Culbone Church. He was writing it down when 'a person on business from Porlock' knocked at the door, and by the time the visitor left, the rest of the poem was gone

name: Farringford, Isle of Wight
note: 丁尼生 1853 年租下法林福德，1856 年买下，此后一直以这里为家，直到 1892 年去世；他在苏塞克斯盖了奥尔德沃斯之后，冬天仍回这里住。2017 年修复后作为历史名宅开放，4 月到 10 月有导览
note_en: Tennyson rented Farringford in 1853, bought it in 1856, and kept it as his home until he died in 1892, spending his winters here after he built a second house, Aldworth, in Sussex. It reopened as a historic house in 2017, with guided tours from April to October
coord_checked: Farringford House, once the home of Tennyson (Geograph photo 6241203, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/6241203, 2026-11-05

name: St Andrew's Church, Clevedon
name_zh: 克利夫登 · 圣安德鲁教堂
note: 布里斯托尔海峡边小山上的老教堂，塞文河口就在这里入海。丁尼生最好的朋友阿瑟·哈勒姆，也就是《悼念集》标题里的 A.H.H.，葬在这里
note_en: This old church stands on a hill above the Bristol Channel, where the Severn estuary opens out into the sea. Arthur Hallam, Tennyson's closest friend and the A.H.H. of In Memoriam, is buried here

name: St Marylebone Parish Church
note: 罗伯特·勃朗宁和伊丽莎白·巴雷特 1846 年在这里结婚。教堂在战争中受损，1949 年重新开放时设了一间勃朗宁礼拜堂纪念这场婚礼，教区至今保存着他们的结婚证书
note_en: Robert Browning and Elizabeth Barrett were secretly married here in 1846. When the church reopened in 1949 after being damaged in the war, it added a Browning Chapel in honour of the wedding, and the parish still has their marriage certificate
coord_checked: St Marylebone Parish Church (Wikipedia), grid ref TQ 28285 82034 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Marylebone_Parish_Church, 2026-11-05

name: Temple Church and the Temple
note: 圣殿骑士团在英格兰的总部教堂，圆形，1185 年祝圣。周围舰队街和泰晤士河之间的圣殿区，现在属于内殿和中殿两所律师学院——正是斯宾塞诗里取代了圣殿骑士的“好学的律师”
note_en: The Knights Templar built this round church as their headquarters in England, and it was consecrated in 1185. The area around it, between Fleet Street and the Thames, now belongs to two of London's ancient law societies, the Inner Temple and the Middle Temple: the lawyers who, as Spenser put it, took the Templars' place
coord_checked: Temple Church (Commons photo 'Temple Church 5, London, UK - Diliff', camera location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Temple_Church_5,_London,_UK_-_Diliff.jpg, 2026-11-05

name: John Clare Cottage, Helpston
name_zh: 赫尔普斯顿 · 约翰·克莱尔小屋
note: 克莱尔 1793 年生在林门街 12 号这座茅草屋里。赫尔普斯顿周围的田野、公地，以及公地被圈占的经过，贯穿他的诗；他葬在村里的圣博托尔夫教堂墓园。约翰·克莱尔基金会 2005 年买下小屋并加以修复，现在对外开放
note_en: John Clare was born in this thatched cottage at 12 Woodgate in 1793. The fields and commons around Helpston, and the way they were fenced off and enclosed, run all through his poetry. He is buried in St Botolph's churchyard in the village. The John Clare Trust bought the cottage in 2005 and has restored it
coord_checked: John Clare Cottage, Helpston (Geograph photo 3945475, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/3945475, 2026-11-05

name: Shandy Hall, Coxwold
name_zh: 考克斯沃尔德 · 项狄府
note: 斯特恩 1760 至 1768 年在考克斯沃尔德当牧师，住在这里，写了《项狄传》后面几卷和《感伤的旅行》；《项狄传》头两卷在他搬来以前已经出版。现由劳伦斯·斯特恩基金会管理，对外开放
note_en: Laurence Sterne lived here from 1760 to 1768 while he was the curate of Coxwold. The first two volumes of Tristram Shandy were already out, and he wrote the rest of it here, along with A Sentimental Journey. The house is run by the Laurence Sterne Trust and is open to visitors

name: Carlyle's House, Chelsea
name_zh: 切尔西 · 卡莱尔故居
note: 托马斯和简·卡莱尔 1834 年搬进切恩街 24 号，一直住到他 1881 年去世。他在这里写了《法国革命史》和此后的大部分作品。现归国民信托所有
note_en: Thomas and Jane Carlyle lived at 24 Cheyne Row from 1834 until his death in 1881. He wrote The French Revolution here, along with most of his later work. The house is owned by the National Trust
coord_checked: Nos 16 to 22, No 24 Carlyle's House and Nos 26 to 34 Cheyne Row (British Listed Buildings, Grade II*) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101358142-16-22-24-carlyles-house-and-26-34-cheyne-row-royal-hospital-ward, 2026-11-05

name: Cowper and Newton Museum, Olney
name_zh: 奥尔尼 · 柯珀与牛顿博物馆
note: 柯珀 1768 至 1786 年住在集市广场边的果园居。他和写《奇异恩典》的牧师约翰·牛顿合写了《奥尔尼圣诗》，1783 年又开始写长诗《任务》，诗里的风景就是小镇周围的乌斯河谷。房子现在是柯珀与牛顿博物馆
note_en: William Cowper lived at Orchard Side, on the market square, from 1768 to 1786. Together with the local curate John Newton, the man who wrote Amazing Grace, he wrote the Olney Hymns. In 1783 he began his long poem The Task, which looks out over the Ouse valley around the town. The house is now the Cowper and Newton Museum
coord_checked: Cowper & Newton Museum, Market Place, Olney (Geograph photo 6856872, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/6856872, 2026-11-05

name: Yr Ysgwrn, Trawsfynydd
name_zh: 特劳斯维尼兹 · 伊斯古恩农场
note: 威尔士诗人赫德·温在普里索谷这座山间农场长大。他 1917 年 7 月战死在帕斯尚尔，几周后他的长诗《英雄》在全国诗歌节上夺得诗人椅，台上的空椅子被盖上黑布。这把“黑椅子”至今放在农场里，农场已由国家公园买下，对外开放
note_en: The Welsh poet Hedd Wyn grew up on this hill farm in Cwm Prysor. He was killed at Passchendaele in July 1917, and a few weeks later his poem Yr Arwr won the chair at the National Eisteddfod; when no one stood up to claim it, the empty chair was draped in black. The Black Chair is still here, and the farm, now owned by the national park, is open to visitors
coord_checked: Yr Ysgwrn, home of the poet Hedd Wyn (Commons photo by Alan Fryer, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AYr_Ysgwrn%2C_cartref_y_bardd_Hedd_Wyn_-_Yr_Ysgwrn%2C_home_of_the_poet_Hedd_Wyn_-_geograph.org.uk_-_3704246.jpg, 2026-11-05

name: Seamus Heaney HomePlace, Bellaghy
name_zh: 贝拉希 · 谢默斯·希尼故里中心
note: 介绍希尼生平和作品的艺术中心，2016 年在贝拉希开幕；他家 1953 年搬到这个村子。他 1939 年生在卡斯尔道森附近的家族农场莫斯鲍恩，葬在村里的圣玛利亚教堂墓园，墓碑上写着“不顾理智，在空中行走”
note_en: This arts centre, opened in 2016, tells the story of Seamus Heaney's life and work. It's in Bellaghy, where his family moved in 1953. He was born in 1939 at Mossbawn, the family farm near Castledawson, and he's buried in St Mary's churchyard here in the village, under the words 'Walk on air against your better judgement'

name: Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre, Great Missenden
name_zh: 大米森登 · 罗尔德·达尔博物馆
note: 达尔在大米森登的吉普赛屋住了 36 年，直到 1990 年去世。博物馆设在高街上一座旧驿站客栈里，2005 年开幕，收藏着他的手稿和文件
note_en: Roald Dahl lived at Gipsy House in Great Missenden for thirty-six years, until he died in 1990. The museum, in an old coaching inn on the High Street, opened in 2005 and holds his archive
coord_checked: The Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre (Geograph photo 1264147, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/1264147, 2026-11-05

name: The sweet shop, 11 High Street, Llandaff
name_zh: 兰达夫 · 高街 11 号糖果店
note: 《好小子》里“老鼠大阴谋”发生的糖果店。1924 年，七岁的达尔和四个伙伴把一只死老鼠放进了这里的硬糖罐；店主后来成了书里的普拉切特太太。2009 年挂上了蓝色纪念牌
note_en: This is the sweet shop from the Great Mouse Plot in Boy. In 1924, seven-year-old Roald Dahl and four friends slipped a dead mouse into a jar of gobstoppers here. The shopkeeper became the horrible Mrs Pratchett in the book. A blue plaque went up in 2009

name: Repton School
prototype_of: 不是工厂本身：1930 年代达尔在雷普顿上学时，和同学们一起替吉百利试吃新出的巧克力，他梦想将来给吉百利发明巧克力。他说《查理和巧克力工厂》就是从这里来的
prototype_of_en: There was never a chocolate factory here, but when Dahl was at Repton in the 1930s, Cadbury sent the boys boxes of new chocolate bars to test. He dreamed of one day working as an inventor in Cadbury's lab, and he said that was where Charlie and the Chocolate Factory came from

name: Exeter College, Oxford
name_zh: 牛津 · 埃克塞特学院
prototype_of: 普尔曼自己读书的学院，也是《黑暗物质》里乔丹学院的原型：莱拉从小在乔丹的屋顶上乱跑，那座学院就站在埃克塞特的位置上，格局也照着它，只是更大、更富、更古老。学院下午对游客开放，可以看哥特式的礼拜堂，从院士花园望见拉德克利夫圆顶
prototype_of_en: Exeter was Philip Pullman's own college, and it's the model for Jordan College in His Dark Materials, where Lyra runs wild across the rooftops. Jordan stands exactly where Exeter does and follows its layout, only bigger, richer and older. The college is open to visitors in the afternoons, and you can see the Gothic chapel and look out from the Fellows' Garden onto the Radcliffe Camera

name: The bench in the Oxford Botanic Garden
note: 英国最古老的植物园，建于 1621 年。园子后面那张长椅——威尔和莱拉约定每年仲夏日去坐的地方——成了读者的朝圣地；2019 年起，长椅后面立着朱利安·沃伦的雕塑
note_en: Founded in 1621, this is the oldest botanic garden in Britain. The bench at the back of the garden, where Will and Lyra promise to come and sit every Midsummer's Day, has become a pilgrimage site for readers. Since 2019 a sculpture by Julian Warren has stood behind it

name: Watership Down
note: 《兔子共和国》（又译《沃特希普荒原》）以这座白垩丘陵命名：小兔榛子和预言家小五带着伙伴们逃离即将被毁的家园，一路跋涉来到这里建立新的养兔场。理查德·亚当斯是在带女儿们开车出游的路上给她们讲出这个故事的
note_en: Watership Down takes its name from this chalk hill. Hazel and his brother Fiver, who can sense when danger is coming, lead a small band of rabbits away from their doomed warren and make the long journey here to start a new one. Richard Adams first made up the story to entertain his daughters on long car trips
coord_checked: Watership Down (Geograph photo 3111, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/3111, 2026-11-05

name: The World of James Herriot, Thirsk
name_zh: 瑟斯克 · 吉米·哈利的世界
note: 以吉米·哈利（James Herriot）为笔名写作的阿尔夫·怀特，住在柯克盖特 23 号并在这里行医；书里它是斯凯尔代尔宅，达罗比镇则是瑟斯克、里士满、莱伯恩和米德尔赫姆几个小镇的合体。1999 年改为博物馆开放
note_en: Alf Wight, who wrote as James Herriot, lived and worked as a vet at 23 Kirkgate. In his books it's Skeldale House, and the town of Darrowby is a mix of Thirsk, Richmond, Leyburn and Middleham. The house opened as a museum in 1999
coord_checked: The World of James Herriot (Geograph photo 636931, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/636931, 2026-11-05

name: Charles Dickens Birthplace Museum, Portsmouth
name_zh: 朴茨茅斯 · 狄更斯出生地博物馆
note: 狄更斯 1812 年生在朴茨茅斯这座房子里，父亲当时在海军军需处做小职员。房子按他出生时的样子布置，还陈列着他 1870 年在盖兹山庄去世时躺的那张沙发
note_en: Charles Dickens was born in this Portsmouth house in 1812, when his father was a clerk in the Navy Pay Office. The house is furnished as it would have looked at the time, and it also holds the sofa on which Dickens died at his home in Kent in 1870

name: Max Gate, Dorchester
name_zh: 多切斯特 · 马克斯门
note: 哈代自己设计了这座房子，由他的父亲和弟弟施工。他 1885 年住进来，直到 1928 年去世，在这里写了《德伯家的苔丝》《无名的裘德》《卡斯特桥市长》和大量的诗。1940 年他的妹妹凯特把房子留给了国民信托
note_en: Hardy designed this house himself, and his father and brother built it. He lived here from 1885 until he died in 1928, and he wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Jude the Obscure, The Mayor of Casterbridge and much of his poetry here. His sister Kate left it to the National Trust in 1940

name: Samuel Johnson Birthplace Museum, Lichfield
name_zh: 利奇菲尔德 · 约翰逊出生地博物馆
note: 约翰逊的父亲迈克尔是书商，1707 年盖了这座房子，楼下开书店、楼上住家；约翰逊 1709 年 9 月 18 日生在这里。房子在市场街和面包市场街的拐角，对着集市广场，1901 年起是博物馆
note_en: Samuel Johnson's father, Michael, was a bookseller, and he built this house in 1707 as both his shop and his home. Johnson was born here on 18 September 1709. The house stands on the corner of Market Street and Breadmarket Street, facing the market square, and has been a museum since 1901

name: Bateman's, Burwash
name_zh: 伯沃什 · 贝特曼庄园
note: 吉卜林夫妇 1902 年买下贝特曼庄园，他在这里一直住到 1936 年去世。《普克山的帕克》就是以从屋里望得见的那座小山命名的，《如果》也是在这里写的。1939 年按他遗孀卡罗琳的遗嘱归国民信托
note_en: Rudyard Kipling and his wife bought Bateman's in 1902, and he lived here until his death in 1936. Puck of Pook's Hill is named after the hill you can see from the house, and he wrote If— here too. When his widow, Caroline, died, the house passed to the National Trust in 1939

name: Rydal Mount
note: 华兹华斯 1813 年搬来，在这里一直住到 1850 年去世。他的玄孙女玛丽·亨德森 1969 年买下这里，1970 年对外开放；2026 年华兹华斯基金会买下了它
note_en: This was Wordsworth's home from 1813 until he died in 1850. His great-great-granddaughter Mary Henderson bought it in 1969 and opened it to the public the following year. The Wordsworth Trust bought it in 2026

name: Robert Burns House, Dumfries
name_zh: 邓弗里斯 · 彭斯故居
note: 彭斯生命最后三年住在这座红砂岩小楼里，1796 年在这里去世，年仅三十七岁。他最后的诗作和歌谣大多写于此。故居现为博物馆，几步之外的圣米迦勒教堂墓园里是他的陵墓
note_en: Robert Burns spent the last three years of his life in this small red sandstone house and died here in 1796, aged only thirty-seven. Many of his last poems and songs were written here. It's now a museum, and his mausoleum is just a short walk away in St Michael's churchyard
coord_checked: 24 Burns Street, Robert Burns House (British Listed Buildings, Category A) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/200362606-24-burns-street-robert-burns-house-dumfries, 2026-11-05

name: J. M. Barrie's Birthplace, Kirriemuir
name_zh: 基里缪尔 · 巴里出生地
note: 巴里 1860 年 5 月 9 日生在布里金路 9 号，是织布工家里十个孩子中的第九个。七岁时，他在屋后的洗衣房里排演了自己的第一出戏，据说《彼得·潘》里的温迪小屋就是从这里来的。现由苏格兰国民信托管理
note_en: J. M. Barrie was born at 9 Brechin Road on 9 May 1860, the ninth of ten children in a family of weavers. When he was seven, he put on his first play in the wash-house out the back, which is said to have inspired the Wendy House in Peter Pan. The National Trust for Scotland looks after it
coord_checked: J. M. Barrie's birthplace, Kirriemuir (Geograph photo 2513632, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/2513632, 2026-11-05

name: Dylan Thomas Birthplace, 5 Cwmdonkin Drive, Swansea
name_zh: 斯旺西 · 迪伦·托马斯出生地
note: 迪伦·托马斯 1914 年生在斯旺西高地区这座房子的前卧室，一直住到 1937 年父母搬走。房子已按 1914 年的样子修复，对外开放
note_en: Dylan Thomas was born in the front bedroom of this house in the Uplands area of Swansea in 1914, and he lived here until his parents moved out in 1937. It has been restored to look the way it did in 1914 and is open to visitors
coord_checked: Birthplace of Dylan Thomas in Swansea (Geograph photo 4091841, subject location) — https://www.geograph.org.uk/photo/4091841, 2026-11-05

name: C. S. Lewis Square, Belfast
name_zh: 贝尔法斯特 · C. S. 刘易斯广场
note: 贝尔法斯特东区的一个广场，在康斯沃特绿道和科默绿道交会处；刘易斯就在东区长大。广场 2016 年 11 月 22 日落成，正是他去世 53 周年，广场上有莫里斯·哈伦雕的七座《狮子、女巫和魔衣橱》人物雕像
note_en: This square in east Belfast, where C. S. Lewis grew up, sits where the Connswater and Comber Greenways meet. It opened on 22 November 2016, fifty-three years to the day after his death, with seven bronze sculptures by Maurice Harron of characters from The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
coord_checked: C S Lewis Square and sculpture trail, Belfast (Commons photo by Simon Burchell, camera location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AC_S_Lewis_Square_and_sculpture_trail%2C_Belfast_01.jpg, 2026-11-05

name: Moseley Bog, Birmingham
name_zh: 伯明翰 · 莫斯利沼泽
prototype_of: 托尔金小时候就住在附近，后来说这一带是“一种失落的乐园”。他承认，《霍比特人》和《魔戒》里那些古老的森林，灵感来自这片老树林。现在是自然保护区，由伯明翰与黑乡野生动物信托管理
prototype_of_en: Tolkien lived near here as a boy and later called this countryside 'a kind of lost paradise'. He said these old woods helped inspire the ancient forests of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Today it's a nature reserve run by the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country

name: 20 Northmoor Road, Oxford
name_zh: 牛津 · 北沼路 20 号
note: 托尔金 1930 至 1947 年的家。文物登录说明里写着，他在这座房子里写了《霍比特人》的全部和《魔戒》的几乎全部。现在是私宅，2004 年列为二级保护建筑，墙上有蓝色纪念牌
note_en: This was Tolkien's home from 1930 to 1947. According to its official listing, he wrote all of The Hobbit and almost all of The Lord of the Rings in this house. It's a private home, with a blue plaque outside, and has been a Grade II listed building since 2004
coord_checked: 20 Northmoor Road (British Listed Buildings, Grade II) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101391361-20-northmoor-road-oxford, 2026-11-05

name: Anna Sewell's House, Great Yarmouth
name_zh: 大雅茅斯 · 安娜·休厄尔故居
note: 安娜·休厄尔 1820 年 3 月 30 日生在教堂广场 26 号。《黑骏马》是她多年以后在诺里奇附近老卡顿的家里写的，从 1871 年写到 1877 年；书出版几个月后，她于 1878 年去世。现在这座房子由红翼马匹救助站租用，2022 年起对外开放
note_en: Anna Sewell was born at 26 Church Plain on 30 March 1820. She wrote Black Beauty much later, between 1871 and 1877, at her home in Old Catton near Norwich, and she died in 1878, just a few months after the book came out. The Redwings Horse Sanctuary leases the house and opened it to visitors in 2022
coord_checked: Anna Sewell's House, Church Plain, Great Yarmouth (Commons photo by Colin Smith, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3A-2020-08-17_Anna_Sewell%E2%80%99s_House%2C_Church_Plain%2C_Great_Yarmouth%2C_Norfolk.jpg, 2026-11-05

name: Douglas Adams's grave, Highgate Cemetery
name_zh: 海格特公墓 · 道格拉斯·亚当斯墓
note: 《银河系漫游指南》的作者道格拉斯·亚当斯 2001 年突然去世，葬在海格特公墓东园。墓很好认：书迷们在墓前插满了一罐笔，有时还会留一条毛巾——书里说过，搭车漫游银河的人一定要带毛巾。离乔治·艾略特和马克思的墓都不远
note_en: Douglas Adams, author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, died suddenly in 2001 and is buried in the East Cemetery at Highgate. His grave is easy to find: fans keep it stocked with a pot of pens, and sometimes leave a towel, since every galactic hitchhiker knows where theirs is. George Eliot and Karl Marx are just a short walk away
coord_checked: Douglas Adams's grave (Geograph 5847972 on Commons, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ADouglas_Adams_-_geograph.org.uk_-_5847972.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: Guildford
note: 《银河系漫游指南》里，福特·普里菲克特在地球上待了十五年，一直让人以为他是吉尔福德来的失业演员——其实他来自参宿四附近的一颗小行星。道格拉斯·亚当斯挑了一座最普通的英国郡城做这个玩笑
note_en: In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Ford Prefect spends fifteen years on Earth pretending to be an out-of-work actor from Guildford. In reality he's from a small planet somewhere near Betelgeuse. Douglas Adams picked one of the most ordinary towns in England for the joke
coord_checked: Guildford High Street (Geograph 3968888 on Commons, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AGuildford_High_Street_-_geograph.org.uk_-_3968888.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: Wells Cathedral
prototype_of: 肯·福莱特说，《圣殿春秋》里王桥大教堂的原型是韦尔斯和索尔兹伯里两座大教堂。韦尔斯大教堂 12 世纪末开工，是英国第一座通体哥特式的教堂，正好是小说里的年代。今天可以看正面的三百多尊雕像、中殿交叉的“剪刀拱”和 14 世纪的天文钟
prototype_of_en: Ken Follett has said that Kingsbridge Cathedral in The Pillars of the Earth was inspired by the cathedrals at Wells and Salisbury. Wells was begun in the late twelfth century, the novel's own era, and was the first cathedral in England built entirely in the Gothic style. Today you can see the three hundred figures on the west front, the great scissor arches at the crossing, and a fourteenth-century astronomical clock

name: Deptford
note: 《晚安，汤姆先生》里，二战疏散儿童威廉·比奇就是从德特福德被送到乡下的，后来又回到这里，在母亲的公寓里发生了全书最黑暗的一幕。早在 1593 年，剧作家马洛也是在德特福德的一间屋子里被刺死的
note_en: In Goodnight Mister Tom, the young evacuee William Beech is sent to the countryside from Deptford, and later he has to come back here, to his mother's flat, for the darkest part of the book. Deptford has an even older literary story: in 1593 the playwright Christopher Marlowe was stabbed to death in a house here

name: Lelant, Cornwall
note: 皮尔彻 1924 年生在这个村子，村子在圣艾夫斯附近的海尔河口。西南海岸步道介绍她的康沃尔的页面说，《拾贝人》的故事发生在伦敦和莱兰特
note_en: Rosamunde Pilcher was born in this village on the Hayle estuary, near St Ives, in 1924. According to the South West Coast Path's guide to her Cornwall, The Shell Seekers is set partly in London and partly here in Lelant

name: Peel Island, Coniston Water
name_zh: 科尼斯顿湖 · 皮尔岛
prototype_of: 野猫岛的原型之一。兰塞姆八岁时在这座岛上野餐，第一次认识了科林伍德一家；后来这家人的孙辈成了“燕子号”孩子们的原型之一。岛属于国民信托
prototype_of_en: Peel Island is one of the models for Wild Cat Island in Swallows and Amazons. Arthur Ransome first met the Collingwood family at a picnic here when he was eight, and years later their grandchildren helped inspire the Swallows. The island belongs to the National Trust
coord_checked: Peel Island, Coniston Water (Geograph 5213528 on Commons, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3APeel_Island%2C_Coniston_Water_-_geograph.org.uk_-_5213528.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: Site of Green Hedges, Beaconsfield
name_zh: 比肯斯菲尔德 · 绿篱旧址
note: 布莱顿 1938 年搬进彭路上的“绿篱”，英格兰遗产委员会说她的大部分书是在这里写的；魔法树系列 1939 至 1951 年陆续出版，正是她住在这里的时候。房子 1973 年拆掉，原址现在是布莱顿巷
note_en: Enid Blyton moved to Green Hedges on Penn Road in 1938, and according to English Heritage she wrote most of her books here. The Faraway Tree books all came out while she lived in this house, between 1939 and 1951. The house was knocked down in 1973, and a street called Blyton Close now stands on the site
coord_checked: Blyton Close, Beaconsfield, HP9 2LX (Doogal postcode map) — https://www.doogal.co.uk/ShowMap.php?postcode=HP9%202LX, 2026-11-07

name: Hastings
prototype_of: 《穿破裤子的慈善家》里的马格斯伯勒就是黑斯廷斯。特雷塞尔在这里给建筑和装修商做工，小说大部分写在圣伦纳兹伦敦路 241 号的顶层公寓里，门边有纪念牌
prototype_of_en: Mugsborough, the town in The Ragged Trousered Philanthropists, is really Hastings. Robert Tressell worked for builders and decorators here, and he wrote most of the novel in a top-floor flat at 241 London Road, St Leonards, which now has a plaque

name: The Globe, Bedale Street, Borough
scene: 布里奇特的公寓，就在博罗市场边环球酒馆的楼上：她在这里写日记、数卡路里、等电话，片尾还在楼下的雪地里追出门去。酒馆至今照常营业，楼下的博罗市场是伦敦最老的食品市场之一，周末挤满了吃小吃的人
scene_en: Bridget's flat, above the Globe pub by Borough Market, where she writes her diary, counts calories and waits for the phone to ring, and at the end runs out into the snow after Mark. The pub is still open for business, and Borough Market downstairs, one of the oldest food markets in London, is packed with people grazing at the stalls on weekends
coord_checked: The Globe, Borough (Commons photo, camera location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AGlobe%2C_Borough%2C_SE1_%282386237082%29.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: Platt's Lane, Hampstead
name_zh: 汉普斯特德 · 普拉茨巷
note: 威尔基·柯林斯学会按书中的路线考证，沃尔特·哈特赖特穿过汉普斯特德荒野的那次夜行，就走到了这个路口：当年写作 Pratts Lane、今天叫普拉茨巷的小路，在这里接上芬奇利路
note_en: The Wilkie Collins Society worked out that Walter Hartright's night walk across Hampstead Heath in The Woman in White ends here, where Pratts Lane (now Platt's Lane) meets Finchley Road. It's where he meets the mysterious woman in white

name: Wingfield Castle, Suffolk
name_zh: 萨福克 · 温菲尔德城堡
prototype_of: 《我的秘密城堡》里莫特曼一家住的“天赐城堡”，原型就是这座城堡：书里一家人穷得叮当响，住在半倒塌的中世纪城堡里，17 岁的卡桑德拉坐在水槽里写日记。真城堡 14 世纪建成，四面有护城河，门楼是原物。现在是私宅，不对外开放
prototype_of_en: Wingfield Castle inspired Godsend Castle in I Capture the Castle, the half-ruined medieval home of the penniless Mortmain family, where seventeen-year-old Cassandra writes her journal sitting in the kitchen sink. The real castle dates from the fourteenth century and is surrounded by a moat, with its original gatehouse still standing. It's a private home and isn't open to the public

name: Puttenham Common, Surrey
name_zh: 萨里 · 帕特纳姆公地
note: 法纳姆和吉尔福德之间的一片荒地和树林，在帕特纳姆村南边，往埃尔斯特德方向。书里野人住的灯塔是虚构的，但书里说它在帕特纳姆和埃尔斯特德之间的山头上，北面是猪背岭
note_en: This stretch of heath and woodland lies between Farnham and Guildford, south of the village of Puttenham and towards Elstead. The Savage's lighthouse in Brave New World is made up, but Huxley places it on a hill between Puttenham and Elstead, with the Hog's Back ridge to the north
coord_checked: Puttenham Common (Geograph 4027729 on Commons, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3APuttenham_Common_-_geograph.org.uk_-_4027729.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: The Lady, 39–40 Bedford Street, Covent Garden
name_zh: 考文特花园 · 《淑女》杂志旧址
note: 吉本斯在《淑女》杂志做编辑助理，《寒冷舒适农场》就是她在杂志社考文特花园办公室里抽空写的；一位同事记得她为了写小说常常耽误本职工作。《淑女》杂志在贝德福德街 39–40 号一直待到 2019 年
note_en: Stella Gibbons was an editorial assistant at The Lady magazine, and she wrote Cold Comfort Farm in her spare moments at its offices in Covent Garden. One colleague remembered her neglecting her actual work to get on with the novel. The Lady was based at 39–40 Bedford Street until 2019

name: Lincoln Cathedral
prototype_of: 安雅·塞顿《凯瑟琳》的主人公凯瑟琳·斯温福德确有其人，晚年住在大教堂的教堂区里。她和女儿琼·博福特合葬在这里，墓在天使唱诗堂的南侧
prototype_of_en: The real Katherine Swynford, the heroine of Anya Seton's novel Katherine, lived in the cathedral close in her later years. She's buried in the cathedral with her daughter, Joan Beaufort, on the south side of the Angel Choir

name: Crown House, Great Missenden
prototype_of: 罗尔德·达尔在大米森登住了三十多年，村子里处处是他书里的影子。按达尔博物馆村庄步道的说法，高街 70 号这座木结构老房子就是《好心眼儿巨人》里苏菲住的孤儿院，巨人就是在这里把她从窗口抱走的。现在是私宅，只能在街上看，博物馆就在同一条街上
prototype_of_en: Roald Dahl lived in Great Missenden for more than thirty years, and the village turns up all through his books. According to the Roald Dahl Museum's village trail, this timber-framed house at 70 High Street is the orphanage in The BFG, where the giant snatches Sophie from her window. It's a private home, so you can only look from the street, and the museum is just along the same road
coord_checked: Crown House, Great Missenden (British Listed Buildings, Grade II) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101124792-crown-house-great-missenden, 2026-11-07

name: Great Missenden Library
prototype_of: 达尔博物馆的村庄步道说，这就是玛蒂尔达常来的那座图书馆：妈妈去艾尔斯伯里打宾果，四岁的她就独自走来，把儿童书架读完了，又开始读狄更斯。现在的房子建于 1970 年，仍是村里的公共图书馆，可以进去坐坐
prototype_of_en: According to the Roald Dahl Museum's village trail, this is the library Matilda walks to on her own while her mother is off playing bingo in Aylesbury. At four years old she reads her way through the children's shelves and moves on to Dickens. The present building dates from 1970, and it's still the village's public library, so you can drop in
coord_checked: Great Missenden Library (Geograph 8112772 on Commons, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AGreat_Missenden_Library_-_geograph.org.uk_-_8112772.jpg, 2026-11-07

name: Buckingham House, Old Portsmouth
name_zh: 老朴茨茅斯 · 白金汉府
note: 高街 11 号，1628 年 8 月 23 日白金汉公爵在这里被约翰·费尔顿刺死，大仲马在《三个火枪手》结尾重写了这件事。房子建于 16 世纪，木结构，后来做过客栈，现在是办公室和公寓，墙上有纪念牌
note_en: On 23 August 1628, the Duke of Buckingham was stabbed to death in this house at 11 High Street by a disgruntled officer named John Felton. Dumas retells the murder at the end of The Three Musketeers. The sixteenth-century timber-framed building later became an inn and is now offices and flats, with a plaque on the wall recording the assassination
coord_checked: Buckingham House, 10½–11 High Street (British Listed Buildings, Grade II*) — https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101104356-buckingham-house-st-thomas-ward, 2026-11-09

name: Savile Row
note: 伦敦的高级裁缝街。凡尔纳让福格住在萨维尔街 7 号，一个生活精确到秒的绅士，就是从这里出发去打那个赌的。凡尔纳说这正是剧作家谢里丹去世的房子，其实谢里丹死在同一条街的 17 号
note_en: Savile Row is London's street of bespoke tailors. Jules Verne gave Phileas Fogg, a man who lives his life to the exact second, a house at number 7, and it's from here that he sets off on his famous bet. Verne claims it was the house where the playwright Richard Sheridan died, although Sheridan actually died at number 17
coord_checked: No 3 Savile Row (Commons photo, object location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ANo_3%2C_Savile_Row_door_and_sign.jpg, 2026-11-09

name: Liverpool
note: 《八十天环游地球》里，福格从美洲回来在利物浦上岸，离伦敦只差六个小时、期限还剩不到一天，却被一路追踪他的菲克斯警探当场逮捕，差点输掉一切
note_en: In Around the World in Eighty Days, Fogg lands at Liverpool on his way back from America. He is only six hours from London with less than a day to spare, when Detective Fix, who has been following him all the way around the world, arrests him right on the dock

name: Walmer beach, near Deal
name_zh: 迪尔附近 · 沃尔默海滩
note: 恺撒没有写出登陆的地名，只说离开悬崖几英里后是一片开阔平坦的海岸。传统上认为公元前 55 年的登陆地是沃尔默和迪尔之间的卵石滩，海滨有一块纪念牌；2017 年以来的考古发现则把公元前 54 年的登陆地指向更北的佩格韦尔湾
note_en: Julius Caesar doesn't name a beach, only an open, flat shore a few miles past the cliffs. The traditional landing place for his invasion of 55 BC is the shingle beach between Walmer and Deal, where a plaque stands on the seafront. Since 2017, though, archaeologists have pointed to Pegwell Bay, further north, as the site of his second landing in 54 BC
coord_checked: Caesar's first invasion plaque, Walmer (Historical Marker Database) — https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=24553, 2026-11-09

name: Brentford Monument
note: 布伦特福德高街上 1909 年立的花岗岩柱，刻着四件史事，第一件是公元前 54 年恺撒在这里的古渡口渡过泰晤士河、击退卡西维拉努斯。恺撒本人只写了河名；布伦特福德是传统上对那个唯一可涉水之处的考订
note_en: This granite column on Brentford High Street, put up in 1909, records four historic events. The first is Julius Caesar crossing the Thames here in 54 BC to fight the British leader Cassivellaunus. Caesar himself only mentions the river, but Brentford has traditionally been identified as the one place where it could be forded

name: Isle of Portland
note: 《笑面人》开篇：1690 年一个冬夜，一群人贩子乘船逃离英国，把一个十岁的男孩丢在波特兰荒凉的海岸上。男孩在风雪中抱起一个弃婴，走到韦茅斯求救——他就是脸被割成永远微笑的格温普兰
note_en: The Man Who Laughs opens on a winter night in 1690. A gang of child traffickers sails away from England and leaves a ten-year-old boy behind on the bleak coast of Portland. Struggling through the snow, he finds a baby and carries her all the way to Weymouth to get help. The boy is Gwynplaine, whose face has been cut into a permanent grin

name: Southwark
note: 伦敦桥南岸的区，几百年来是伦敦人寻欢的地方，客栈、剧院、斗熊场都在这里。雨果把于尔絮斯的“绿箱子”和塔德卡斯特客栈安排在他虚构于此的塔林佐场
note_en: Southwark, just across London Bridge, was for centuries the city's playground, full of inns, theatres and bear-baiting pits. In The Man Who Laughs, Hugo sets the travelling show of Ursus and the Tadcaster Inn on a fairground here that he calls Tarrinzeau Field

name: Southampton
note: 《黑执事》里，夏尔和塞巴斯蒂安在南安普敦登上开往纽约的豪华邮轮坎帕尼亚号，船上随即发生了一连串诡异事件。现实中 1912 年泰坦尼克号也是从这里出发的
note_en: In Black Butler, Ciel and Sebastian board the luxury liner Campania in Southampton, bound for New York, and things start to go very strangely once they're at sea. In real life, the Titanic set sail from here in 1912

name: Tintagel Castle
note: 康沃尔北岸的海岬城堡，1230 年代由康沃尔伯爵理查所建，但传说早已先占了这块地：蒙茅斯的杰弗里（约 1136 年）把亚瑟的受孕安排在这里，瓦斯、马洛礼、丁尼生都让伊格赖因被困在廷塔杰尔、乌瑟在城外围攻。现由英格兰遗产委员会管理，2019 年起有人行桥通往岛上
note_en: This clifftop castle on the north coast of Cornwall was built in the 1230s by Richard, Earl of Cornwall, on a spot that legend had already claimed. Around 1136, Geoffrey of Monmouth wrote that King Arthur was conceived here, and later Wace, Malory and Tennyson all have Igraine shut away in Tintagel while Uther lays siege to it. It's run by English Heritage, and since 2019 a footbridge has connected the mainland to the island

name: Glastonbury Abbey
note: 1191 年，修士们宣布在这里挖到了亚瑟和桂妮薇儿的墓，现在一般认为是大火后为筹款做的噱头。马洛礼的《亚瑟之死》也在这里收尾：做了隐士的兰斯洛特把桂妮薇儿葬在亚瑟身边。今天修道院只剩废墟，草地上的标志指着 1278 年迁葬的墓址
note_en: In 1191 the monks here announced that they had dug up the grave of Arthur and Guinevere, which is now generally seen as a fundraising stunt after a fire. Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur ends here too, with Lancelot, now a hermit, burying Guinevere beside Arthur. The abbey is in ruins today, and a marker in the grass shows where their tomb was placed in 1278

name: The Great Hall, Winchester
note: 温切斯特城堡只剩这座亨利三世 1222—1235 年建的大厅，墙上挂着那张圆桌。年轮测定圆桌做于 1250—1280 年；亨利八世命人画上亚瑟和骑士们的名字。马洛礼 1460 年代写书时直说卡美洛“用英语说就是温切斯特”
note_en: This great hall, built by Henry III between 1222 and 1235, is all that's left of Winchester Castle, and the Round Table hangs on its wall. Tree-ring dating shows the table was made between 1250 and 1280, and Henry VIII later had it painted with Arthur and the names of his knights. Malory, writing in the 1460s, states plainly that Camelot is Winchester

name: Cadbury Castle, Somerset
name_zh: 萨默塞特 · 卡德伯里城堡
prototype_of: 当地传说认为这座铁器时代的山堡就是亚瑟的卡美洛，1542 年就有人记下了这个说法。20 世纪 60 年代的考古发掘发现，它在公元 500 年前后重新筑防，还建过一座大厅，确实有位后罗马时代的统治者住过。今天可以爬上山顶，沿着几道土垒走一圈，俯瞰萨默塞特平原
prototype_of_en: Local tradition, already written down in 1542, says this Iron Age hill fort was Arthur's Camelot. When archaeologists dug here in the 1960s, they found it had been refortified around the year 500 and given a great hall, so some real post-Roman ruler did hold this hill. You can climb to the top today, walk the rings of earthworks, and look out over the Somerset Levels

name: Dozmary Pool, Bodmin Moor
name_zh: 博德明荒原 · 多兹玛丽池
prototype_of: 投剑的那片水。博德明荒原上的小湖；康沃尔的传说说湖中仙女在这里把剑交给亚瑟，卡姆兰之战后贝德维尔又在这里把剑还回去。丁尼生笔下破礼拜堂旁的“一片大水”是诗人的风景，但康沃尔把它放在这里
prototype_of_en: This small lake on Bodmin Moor is said to be where Excalibur was thrown. Cornish legend says the Lady of the Lake gave Arthur his sword here, and that Bedivere threw it back into this water after the final battle at Camlann. Tennyson's 'great water' beside a ruined chapel is a poet's invention, but this is where Cornwall puts it

name: Lud's Church, Staffordshire
name_zh: 斯塔福德郡 · 卢德教堂
prototype_of: 绿教堂。戴恩河上方一道滑坡裂出的青苔峡谷，长 100 多米、深 18 米。1958 年 R. W. V. 埃利奥特根据诗的西北米德兰方言，提出这里就是高文赴约的绿教堂；诗里“一个老洞，或老岩壁上的一道裂缝”和它很合。韦顿磨坊附近的南托尔洞是另一个候选地
prototype_of_en: This is thought to be the Green Chapel from Sir Gawain and the Green Knight. It's a deep, mossy chasm, more than a hundred metres long and eighteen metres deep, opened up by a landslip above the River Dane. In 1958 the scholar R. W. V. Elliott, working from the poem's north-west Midlands dialect, suggested this was where Gawain comes to meet the Green Knight, and the poem's 'old cave, or a crevice of an old crag' fits it well. A cave at Nan Tor, near Wetton Mill, is the other main candidate

name: Caerleon
note: 乌斯克河畔的罗马军团要塞伊斯卡，圆形剧场、浴场和营房都还看得见。蒙茅斯的杰弗里和随后的瓦斯把它写成亚瑟在五旬节加冕的城市；那座圆形剧场长期被叫作亚瑟的圆桌。丁尼生写《国王叙事诗》时曾住在这里的汉伯里纹章旅店
note_en: Caerleon was the Roman legionary fortress of Isca, on the River Usk, and you can still see its amphitheatre, baths and barracks. Geoffrey of Monmouth, and Wace after him, made it the city where Arthur is crowned at Pentecost, and the amphitheatre has long been known as Arthur's Round Table. Tennyson stayed at the Hanbury Arms here while working on the Idylls of the King

name: Slaughterbridge, on the River Camel
name_zh: 卡默尔河畔 · 斯劳特桥
prototype_of: 传说中的卡姆兰，亚瑟最后一战的战场：瓦斯说那一仗打在卡默尔河上，17 世纪以来人们就把它定在卡默尔福德附近的这座桥。河岸上有一块 6 世纪的刻字石，被叫作亚瑟王石，其实纪念的是一个叫拉提努斯的人。并没有证据证明这里打过仗，旁边就是亚瑟王中心
prototype_of_en: This is said to be Camlann, the site of Arthur's last battle. Wace places it on the River Camel, and since the seventeenth century it has been identified with this bridge near Camelford. A sixth-century inscribed stone on the riverbank is known as King Arthur's Stone, though it actually commemorates a man called Latinus. There's no proof a battle was ever fought here, but the Arthurian Centre stands right beside it
